La fracción activa bloquea la sustancia receptor P / NK1 en los centros eméticos del SNC (nucleus tractus solitarius, área postrema), previniendo la fase tardía de náuseas y vómitos inducidos por quimioterapia (NVCI) que está totalmente controlada por antagonistas 5-HT3 solos. Una dosis única de 150 mg IV administrada en el día 1 cubre la fase completa de retraso (~5 días), eliminando la necesidad de días orales 2-3 cápsulas. Aprobado por la FDA enero 2008 (formulación de dosis única 150 mg: octubre 2008) y EMA enero 2008.

Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that: Piperacillina es una ureidopenicilina que une las proteínas de unión de penicilina (PBP) e inhibe la síntesis de las paredes celulares bacterianas, produciendo una actividad bactericida rápida contra la mayoría de los bacilos Gram-negativos, incluyendo Pseudomonas aeruginosa, la mayoría Enterobacterales, muchos anaerobes y cocci Gram positivo seleccionados. Tazobactam es un inhibidor irreversible de la β-lactamasa (sulfona de ácido penicilánico) que se une e inactiva a las β lactamasas de clase cromósómica A mediadas por plasmosis (EM, SHV, CTX-M ESBLs parcialmente), restaurando la actividad de la piperacilina contra muchos organismos productores de β -lactamasa. Monoterapia empírica de primera línea para neutropenia febril (FN) en la mayoría de los centros por IDSA, ECIL-4 y NCCN debido a la cobertura pseudomonal, actividad anaeróbica y buen perfil de seguridad.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Positive biochemistry triggers MRI abdomen + 68Ga-DOTATATE PET (or I-123 MIBG). Biochemistry directs adrenalectomy / paraganglioma resection planning. ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs curative-intent surgery scheduling in syndromic carriers.

Platinum-resistant ovarian (PROC) is a d: Platinum-resistant ovarian (PROC) is a defining transition point — prognosis worsens markedly (median OS ~12 mo). Sequential single- agent non-platinum chemo: PLD or weekly paclitaxel are preferred backbones; AURELIA (bevacizumab + chemo) improved PFS (HR 0.48) and is the standard if not bev-exposed and no contraindication. Mirvetuximab-soravtansine (MIRASOL) for FRα-high (≥75% by IHC PS2+) PROC: ORR 42% vs chemo 16%, OS benefit confirmed. PARPi at platinum- resistance generally not recommended (low ORR). Direction "intensify" — operationally re-routes plan generation to PROC algorithm rather than 1L choice. CA-125 + imaging confirmation per GCIG criteria.

Pleuropulmonary blastoma is the canonica: Pleuropulmonary blastoma is the canonical DICER1-syndrome cancer — PPB diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. The Type I → Type II → Type III progression model is unique among pediatric cancers in offering a true surveillance-curable precursor lesion (Type I PPB is histologically benign-appearing cystic disease that, if completely resected, has excellent prognosis; if left in situ, may progress to the higher-mortality Type II/III). Treatment by type: Type I — complete surgical resection; close follow-up imaging for new cysts or solid transformation. Type II/III — surgical resection (often combined lobectomy / pneumonectomy with CNS prophylaxis consideration); IVADo (ifosfamide, vincristine, actinomycin-D, doxorubicin) or similar sarcoma-style regimens; CNS-directed therapy for Type III given high CNS-relapse risk. Distinguishing PPB Type I from congenital pulmonary airway malformation (CPAM) — the most common pediatric cystic lung lesion — is the major early-life diagnostic challenge: family history of DICER1-related malignancies + multi-locular or septated cysts argue for PPB over CPAM and should prompt referral to...

Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) with persistent anovulation and resulting chronic unopposed estrogen exposure on endometrial epithelium — endometrial cancer RR ~2.7 (Haoula et al. Hum Reprod Update 2012); earlier age of onset (40s vs typical 60s) common. Often accompanied by obesity + insulin resistance + type-2 diabetes — additional independent endometrial-cancer risk factors that compound risk multiplicatively. Endometrioid (type I) histology predominates. Frequently underrecognized in women relying on hormonal contraception that masks anovulation. Risk modifiable: combined hormonal contraception (estrogen + progestin) OR cyclic progestin OR levonorgestrel IUD restore endometrial protection. Weight loss + metformin (in T2DM/IR PCOS) provide additional risk reduction. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive expansion).

Polyene macrolide that binds ergosterol: Polyene macrolide that binds ergosterol in the fungal cell membrane, forming transmembrane channels that disrupt membrane integrity, allow leakage of intracellular contents (potassium, magnesium), and produce fungicidal activity. Liposomal encapsulation in unilamellar vesicles (~80 nm) preferentially delivers amphotericin to fungal cells via ergosterol affinity while sparing mammalian cell membranes (which contain cholesterol with lower amphotericin affinity), markedly reducing nephrotoxicity, infusion reactions, and electrolyte wasting vs conventional amphotericin B deoxycholate. Broadest spectrum of any antifungal: most Candida (including azole-resistant), Aspergillus (active, fungicidal), Cryptococcus, ENDEMIC mycoses (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides, Sporothrix), AND Mucorales (Mucor, Rhizopus, Lichtheimia, Cunninghamella) — the latter is critical because echinocandins and mo...
Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of: Polyfunctional alkylating agent: each of three ethyleneimine groups generates an aziridinium intermediate that alkylates DNA primarily at N7 of guanine, producing intra-strand and inter-strand cross-links → DNA replication arrest and apoptosis. Active metabolite TEPA (triethylenephosphoramide, formed by hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 desulfuration) contributes equally to cytotoxicity. Highly lipid-soluble — penetrates CNS readily (CSF levels ~100% of plasma), the basis of its central role in PCNSL induction (MATRix), CNS-relapse-risk lymphoma conditioning (TBC = thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide; TT-BCNU), and intrathecal use for leptomeningeal disease.

Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule in: Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms (AKT1, AKT2, AKT3) within the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway. Suppresses downstream phosphorylation of effector substrates (FOXO, GSK3, TSC2, MDM2, 4EBP1 via mTORC1), reducing proliferation and survival signaling and partially reversing endocrine-therapy resistance in HR+ breast cancer driven by PI3K-pathway alterations. Tumors with activating PIK3CA / AKT1 mutations or PTEN loss (~40-50% of HR+/ HER2- mBC after CDK4/6i) are enriched for response. Pivotal evidence CAPItello-291 (HR+/HER2- mBC after AI ± CDK4/6i): capivasertib + fulvestrant vs placebo + fulvestrant — overall mPFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo HR 0.60; in PIK3CA/AKT1/PTEN-altered subgroup mPFS 7.3 vs 3.1 mo HR 0.50. FDA approval Nov 2023 (mutation-restricted).
Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor ty: Potent inhibitor of multiple receptor tyrosine kinases: VEGFR-1/2/3, PDGFR-α/β, c-KIT, FLT3, CSF-1R, RET. Antiangiogenic + direct antiproliferative effects. In pNET: anti-VEGF/PDGF pathway disrupts tumour neovasculature; direct TKI effect on pNET cells that overexpress VEGFR. Pre-existing autoimmune disease is prese: Pre-existing autoimmune disease is present in ~10-15% of patients eligible for ICI therapy; historically excluded from pivotal trials. Real-world data (Abdel-Wahab 2018, 3557 pts) shows 55% experienced irAE flare and ~29% required systemic immunosuppression beyond steroids. Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Pre-treatment LVEF <50% is an absolute c: Pre-treatment LVEF <50% is an absolute contraindication to anthracycline-containing regimens (R-CHOP, Pola-R-CHP, ABVD, BV-AVD, etc.). Cardiotoxicity from doxorubicin is dose-cumulative and often irreversible; starting with already-impaired function risks acute decompensation.
Pre-treatment nutrition optimization (PE: Pre-treatment nutrition optimization (PEG/J-tube, parenteral nutrition bridge) often required. Prednisone plus cabazitaxel or mitoxantr: Prednisona más cabazitaxel o mitoxantrona para la próstata metastática resistente a la castración...
Preferred 1L for advanced/progressive RE: Preferido 1L para el MTC RET-mutante avanzado/progressivo por NCCN (LIBRETTO-531 aleatorizado vs cabozantinib/vandetanib: SLP superior, menos EAs limitantes al tratamiento). LIBRETTTO-001 ORR ~73% en el MCT RET -mutante con DOR mediana no alcanzada. El paciente debe tener enfermedad avanzada/inresecable + progresión estructural sintomática OR calcitonina tiempo de duplicación <2 años. Pralsetinib (ARROW) es el alternativa selectivo RET.
Preferred 1L for the ~95% of advanced SM: Preferred 1L for the ~95% of advanced SM that is KIT D816V+. Indolent SM (ISM) does NOT receive avapritinib at this dose for disease modification — avapritinib 25 mg in moderate-severe symptomatic ISM (PIONEER) is a separate, narrower symptomatic- control indication not authored here.
Preferred 2nd-gen TKI for younger CML pa: Preferred 2nd-gen TKI for younger CML patients targeting deep molecular response + treatment-free remission, OR for Ph+ ALL. AVOID in pulmonary comorbidity (COPD, prior pleural disease, PAH) due to effusion risk.

Preferred 2nd-gen TKI for younger CML patients without CV risk factors targeting deep molecular response + TFR. AVOID in cardiovascular disease (PAOD, prior MI, uncontrolled hypertension), pancreatitis history, diabetes, hyperlipidemia. Strict fasting requirement is non-trivial adherence burden.

Preferred 2nd-gen TKI for younger CML patients without CV risk factors targeting deep molecular response + TFR. AVOID in cardiovascular disease (PAOD, prior MI, uncontrolled hypertension), pancreatitis history, diabetes, hyperlipidemia…
Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).
Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025: Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025 (over ibrutinib due to less cardiac toxicity). ELEVATE-TN (1L CLL): superior PFS vs Clb+O at 5y; ELEVATE-RR (r/r): non-inferior to ibrutinib with better safety. Funding pathway must be confirmed pre-start in Ukraine.
Preferred BTKi over ibrutinib in modern: Preferido BTKi sobre ibrutinib en las directrices modernas de CLL/MCL (ELEVATE-RR para r/r CLL — eficacia comparable, menos eventos de hipertensión cardíaca/). ELEVate-TN: 1L CLL datos también favorables. Ucrania: registrado pero NO reembolsado a través de NSZU — financiación...
Preferred over zoledronate in patients w: Preferido sobre zoledronato en pacientes con insuficiencia renal. Dosificación de metástasis ósea del cáncer distinta de la dosificación de osteoporosis - mantener separado. aclaramiento dental previo al tratamiento crítico para reducir el riesgo de ONJ.
Pregnancy — absolute contraindication to: Pregnancy — absolute contraindication to lenalidomide. Engine blocks both VRd and D-VRd, falls back to bortezomib + dex (Vd).
Preliminary Safety and Tolerability of C: Seguridad y tolerabilidad preliminares de las células T CD19x22 del RAC en pacientes con LNHB de adolescentes y adultos

Prevention-persona BWS confirmed-carrier: Prevención-persona BWS confirmada-portadora RedFlag (predisposición de cáncer pediátrico Ola M). Rutas motoras a PrevenciónPlan para el tumor de Wilms + vigilancia del hepatoblastoma: abdominal US q3mo desde la infancia hasta los 8 años, AFP mensual hasta los 3-4 años, y q3o hasta los 4 años. STUB pendiente de firma de dos clínicas-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-modo. ancla de enfermedad DIS-WILMS utilizado por breve Wave-M; espectro de cáncer de hepatoblastoma observado en la justificación de indicaciones emparejadas.
Prevention-persona Costello syndrome con: Prevención-persona Síndrome de Costello confirmado-portador RedFlag (predisposición de cáncer pediátrico Ola M). Rutas motoras a PrevenciónPlan para la vigilancia embrionaria-sarcoma: abdominal/pelvica US q3-6mo hasta la edad de 8-10, luego citología de orina + vejiga US desde la edad 10 a lo largo de toda la vida. La vigilancia cardíaca es impulsada por la comorbidez y manejada por vía cardiológica emparejada, no esta RF. STUB pendiente de firma de dos-Clínica-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. El anclaje de la enfermedad DIS-SOFT-TISSUE-SARCOMA cubre el SMR embrionario; neuroblastoma + espectro de cáncer de vejiga TCC observado en la justificación de las Indicaciones pareadas.
Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 a: Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic H. pylori (positive UBT / stool antigen / biopsy histology / stool PCR) AND no confirmed gastric malignancy. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending eradication therapy (per IND-H-PYLORI-PREVENTION-ERADICATION) as the etiological-cancer- prevention pathway. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric cancer causation (IARC Group 1): multiple Cochrane meta-analyses show eradication reduces gastric adenocarcinoma incidence (RR ~0.54-0.66, NNT ~15-50 depending on population baseline incidence). Effect is stronger in high-incidence populations and in younger individuals where atrophic gastritis / intestinal metaplasia has not yet developed. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication is the first-line treatment for early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma, with Wotherspoon regression in ~70-80% of cases (especially t(11;18)- negative). This is treatment-persona territory (existing MALT lymphoma in setting of confirmed H. pylori → treatment Indication, not yet authored) — distinct from prevention persona (chronic H. pylori → prevent MALT/adenocarc...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Engine consumption is DEFERRED to v0.2 implementation wave — the PreventionPlan code path does not yet exist; this RF lands as schema-valid declarative content awaiting that wave.
Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red: Prevention-persona RedFlag combining red-meat ≥500g/week + processed-meat ≥50g/day thresholds per WCRF/AICR + IARC Monograph 114. Severity:major because processed-meat exposure is Group-1 carcinogen with population-attributable fraction ~13% for CRC (WCRF/AICR). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary substitution + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Coexists with existing RF-LIFESTYLE-PROCESSED-MEAT-PREVENTION — both may fire.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heter: Prevention-persona RedFlag for ATM heterozygous carriers. Distinction from biallelic A-T phenotype is critical: heterozygotes have cancer predisposition only (no neurologic phenotype). Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + pancreatic surveillance for FDR-of- PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022; prostate awareness for males. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BAP1 synd: Prevención-persona RedFlag para el síndrome de BAP1 historia familiar. STUB pendiente de firma de dos Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BARD1 heterozygous carriers. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance + ovarian symptom-driven workup. NCCN places BARD1 in moderate-elevated breast tier (annual mammography from age 40; consider MRI). Triple-negative subset signal may justify earlier or MRI-inclusive screening in family- history-stratified cohorts. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BHD/FLCN confirmed carriers. Multi- organ surveillance: abdominal MRI q2-3y from age 20 for RCC (avoid radiation; many BHD lesions are hybrid oncocytic + slow-growing); chest HRCT baseline + symptom-driven (spontaneous pneumothorax triggers high-resolution imaging); dermatology q1y for skin surveillance. Nephron-sparing surgery (partial nephrectomy) preferred for ≤3cm renal lesions given multifocal/bilateral disease pattern. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for BRIP1 heterozygous carriers. NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50; no population ovarian cancer screening recommended. Breast surveillance per general-population schedules unless family history independently elevates risk. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinens: Prevention-persona RedFlag for C. sinensis-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. East-Asian endemic belt has 10-50x higher cholangiocarcinoma incidence than non-endemic Western populations. Geographic context: relevant for East-Asian diaspora, immigrants, refugees, adoptees. Companion to RF-OPISTHORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (Mekong-region liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism — identical surveillance protocol).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDH1 / HD: La Gastrectomía Total profiláctica (PTG) recomendada para los portadores de CDH1 / HDGC confirmada por la guía internacional IGCLC 2020. Gastreectomía total profiláctica (PTg) edades 20-30 (intervalo 18-40 por discusión individualizada); la vigilancia endoscópica se reconoce inferior a la PTG (focos de anillo de signo difuso de tipo débilmente visible) pero ofrecido a portadores con declinación de PTG. Portadores femeninos: vigilancia mamaria de tipo BRCA desde la edad 30. STUB pendiente de firma de dos co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CDKN2A-sp: Prevención-persona RedFlag para portadores específicos de CDKN2A (RF geno-específico vs el más amplio RF FAMMM). Vigilancia pancreática por CAPS Consortium 2018/2020: alternancia de EUS + RMN abdominal/MRCP cada 12 meses desde la edad 40 OR 10 años antes PDAC en familia (siempre antes). Vigilancia del melanoma: examen anual de piel de cuerpo completo + dermoscopia desde la idade 10-12; cartografía de fotografía para múltiples moles atípicos. El paciente debe conocer una protección solar agresiva + cohorte CDKn2A a lo largo de toda la vida. STUB pendiente de la firma de dos co-plomo por el CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for CHEK2 heterozygous carriers. Risk estimates vary substantially by variant: truncating > splice > missense. Engine routes to enhanced breast surveillance (annual mammography from age 40 + MRI consideration), modestly tightened CRC screening (colonoscopy from age 40 with q5y interval per NCCN), and prostate awareness from age 40-45 for males with c.1100delC. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for CMMRD con: Prevención-persona RedFlag para CMMRD confirmada cohorte pediátrica portadora. Vigilancia por cuidado para CmmRD (C4CMMRD) consorcio 2014: RMN de cuerpo entero anualmente desde el diagnóstico; RM de cerebro q6mo a partir de la edad 2; colonoscopia q6o a partir del 6; endoscopia GI superior + cápsula de bowel pequeño anual a partir la edad 8; CBC + electroforesis proteica sérico + abdomen de EE.UU. q6 mo. Prueba de cascada de hermanos + confirmación del portador de la RMM parental. Inmunoterapia (anti-PD-1) eficaz en cánceres relacionados con la RMCM establecidos (Bouffet 2016, serie Larkin/CheckMate). STUB pendiente de firma de dos co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 modo dev.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite: Prevention-persona RedFlag for Cronkhite-Canada syndrome. risk_category set to chronic_condition (not genetic) because etiology is acquired autoimmune-like + non-Mendelian. Surveillance: colonoscopy q1-2y from diagnosis; upper endoscopy q1-2y; small-bowel capsule q2y; treat active disease with immunosuppression (prednisone taper + azathioprine maintenance) + nutritional support (protein replacement, electrolyte correction). Mortality reduced markedly with immuno- suppression treatment. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DES in-ut: Prevención-persona RedFlag para la cohorte de exposición in-utero del DES. La vigilancia se intensifica en relación con la población general (pelvis anual con cuidadosa inspección vaginal/cervical; colposcopia si citología anormal; mamografía a umbral de edad más joven por riesgo de modificador NCCN; considerar la RMN de cribado mamario adjunto con doble riesgo). STUB pendiente de firma de dos-Co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for DICER1 co: Prevención-persona RedFlag para la cohorte confirmada de DICER1. Vigilancia pediátrica por Registro Internacional de PPB / Recomendaciones del IDSDB: - TC de tórax q4-6 mo desde el nacimiento hasta los 3 años de edad, q6-12 mo hasta los 8 años. - E.U. abdominal q3-6 mo de nacimiento hasta la edad de 8 años, - Eje de base de los EE.UU. tiroidea por edad, 8 + q3-5 años. Ooforectomía de reducción de riesgo no respaldada para la prevención de Sertoli-Leydig. STUB pendiente de firma de dos co-Lead por CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-driven cancer prevention inmunocompromised hosts. A diferencia del VHC/HBV/H. pylori, no hay un régimen anti-EBV curativo; la vía de prevención es (a) reducir la inmunosupresión cuando sea factible, (b) el rituximab preventivo en pacientes post-transplante con ADN-EB creciente (por guías internacionales de PTLD), (c) monitoreo periódico del ADN-BV. STUB pendiente de revisión Co-Lead. La utilización de un contexto adicional de inmunocompromiso es deliberada — la seroprevalencia de EBV es >90% en adultos inmunosopetentes a nivel mundial, por lo que un RF disparado en EBVI solo universalmente y no proporciona ninguna señal clínica.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Prevention-persona RedFlag para FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB pendiente de firma de dos Co-Lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on HBsAg+ OR detectable HBV-DNA in patient without HCC. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending nucleos(t)ide analog suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HBV-PREVENTION-ANTIVIRAL) + AFP+US HCC surveillance q6mo per AASLD protocol. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchor target DIS-HCC. HBV-associated DLBCL/NHL is also documented in literature but with weaker effect-size data than the HCV-NHL link; covered via the broader NHL prevention surveillance bullet in the antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (existing) which is the treatment-time RF for HBV reactivation during anti-CD20 / chemo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on positive HIV serology in patient without AIDS-defining or HIV-associated malignancy. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Prevención-persona RedFlag para HPRC. STUB pendiente de la firma de dos co-lead.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-driven ATLL prevention. A diferencia del VHC/HBV/H. pylori, no hay un régimen curativo — la intervención es la vigilancia + prevención de la transmisión, no cura. STUB pendiente Co-Lead revisión. Contexto geográfico: las regiones endémicas de HTVV-1 incluyen Japón (sudoccidente), cuenca del Caribe, partes del África subsahariana, partes de América del Sur, Oriente Medio. Ucrania es de baja prevalencia; esta FR es más relevante para los pacientes de la diáspora o aquellos con viajes/origen de regiones endêmicas.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASLD meets AASLD HCC-surveillance threshold (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhotic advanced fibrosis is a gray zone — closer hepatology follow-up but not yet routine surveillance. Major actionable lever: weight loss + cardiometabolic management. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 heterozygous carriers. PALB2 approaches BRCA2 breast-cancer penetrance and warrants BRCA-style surveillance with annual breast MRI + mammography from age 30, plus pancreatic surveillance (EUS or MRI alternating annually from age 50, or 10 years before earliest PDAC in family) for FDR-of-PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022. RRSO discussion deferred to BRCA-style threshold given lower ovarian penetrance. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anovulation endometrial risk. Separated from the broad reproductive RF for clearer routing — PCOS- specific counseling (progestin restoration, metformin, weight loss) is distinct from generic reproductive-history counseling. Symptom-driven endometrial biopsy in any abnormal bleeding ≥6 months of amenorrhea pre-menopausal OR any post-menopausal bleeding. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) — confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings on MRCP or ERCP (multifocal intra-/extra- hepatic biliary strictures with intervening dilatation, beaded appearance) and/or liver biopsy (concentric periductal fibrosis, onion-skin pattern). No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. Prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases: Prodrug hydrolyzed by carboxylesterases to active metabolite SN-38 (~100-1000× more potent than parent). SN-38 stabilizes the topoisomerase-I/DNA cleavable complex, producing single-strand DNA breaks that become lethal double-strand breaks during S-phase replication. SN-38 is glucuronidated by UGT1A1 to inactive SN-38G; patients homozygous for UGT1A1*28 (Gilbert-syndrome variant) or *6 have impaired clearance and severe neutropenia + diarrhea risk — CPIC and FDA label both recommend testing before high-dose use.
Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B: Prodrug requiring hepatic CYP3A4 / CYP2B6 activation to 4-hydroxy- ifosfamide, which decomposes to ifosforamide mustard — the active DNA- alkylating species producing N7-guanine inter-strand crosslinks and apoptosis in proliferating cells. Side-chain oxidation also generates acrolein (urotoxic — drives hemorrhagic cystitis, neutralized by mesna) and chloroacetaldehyde (the principal neurotoxic metabolite responsible for ifosfamide-induced encephalopathy).
Prodrug that is acid-activated in the pa: Prodrug that is acid-activated in the parietal cell secretory canaliculus to a sulfenamide cation, which forms a covalent disulfide bond with cysteine residues of the H+/K+-ATPase (proton pump) and irreversibly inhibits gastric acid secretion. New pump synthesis is required for recovery (≥24 h half-life of effect despite ~1 h plasma half-life). Cancer-prevention relevance: profound gastric acid suppression is required for H. pylori antimicrobial efficacy (clarithromycin and amoxicillin both require near-neutral gastric pH for stability and bactericidal activity) — PPI is the linchpin of triple / quadruple H. pylori eradication regimens.

Provides supplemental elemental calcium: Provides supplemental elemental calcium (~40% by mass of calcium carbonate). Absorbed in proximal small bowel via active vitamin-D- dependent transcellular transport (saturable at low calcium intake) and passive paracellular diffusion (linear with concentration). Cancer-prevention rationale: intraluminal calcium binds free bile acids and free fatty acids in the colon, reducing their proliferative and pro-inflammatory effect on colonic mucosa; additionally calcium modulates epithelial cell proliferation/differentiation via the calcium-sensing receptor. Calcium Polyp Prevention Study (Baron NEJM 1999) and follow-on trials: 1200 mg/day elemental calcium reduced metachronous adenoma recurrence by ~15-20%.

Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly conve: Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly converted to FdUMP, FdUTP, and FUTP. FdUMP forms a stable ternary complex with thymidylate synthase (TS) + reduced folate (leucovorin), depleting dTMP and blocking DNA synthesis. FUTP misincorporation into RNA disrupts pre-mRNA processing; FdUTP misincorporation into DNA produces strand breaks. Backbone of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, FLOT, and capecitabine-bridged regimens. Bolus and continuous-infusion (CIV) schedules differ in toxicity profile (more myelosuppression with bolus, more mucositis/HFS with CIV).
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporate: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporated into DNA and RNA, inhibits DNA methyltransferases → re-expression of silenced tumor-suppressor genes + cytotoxicity at higher doses. Backbone of MDS-HR, AML-unfit (with venetoclax), and CMML 1L therapy.
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase (rate-limiting) to active metabolites gemcitabine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and triphosphate (dFdCTP). dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxynucleotide pools required for DNA synthesis (self-potentiation effect — increases cellular dFdCTP). dFdCTP is incorporated into DNA, after which one additional natural nucleotide is added before DNA polymerase stalls — "masked chain termination" — making the lesion resistant to exonucleolytic repair. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. PDAC backbone (gem-nab-pac MPACT, gem mono in frail), biliary tract cancers, NSCLC, bladder, NK/T-nasal lymphoma (SMILE), Hodgkin / DLBCL salvage (GDP).
Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after: Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after intracellular polyglutamation by folylpolyglutamate synthetase, simultaneously inhibits multiple folate-dependent enzymes critical for thymidine and purine biosynthesis: thymidylate synthase (TS — primary target), dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase (GARFT). The combined inhibition disrupts both thymidylate and purine de-novo synthesis, halting DNA / RNA production and producing S-phase-specific cytotoxicity. Activity is histology-restricted: highly active in non-squamous NSCLC and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM); minimal-to-no activity in squamous NSCLC due to higher baseline TS expression in squamous histology. Quantitative HBV DNA tracks response during nucleos(t)ide-analogue (NA) therapy with entecavir (ETV) or tenofovir alafenamide/disoproxil (TAF/TDF). Effective suppression (HBV DNA <2,000 IU/mL, ideally undetectable) is the primary virologic response endpoint per AASLD HBV 2024 and EASL HBV 2025. Sustained suppression reduces HCC incidence by ~50-70% in CHB cirrhotics (REVEAL-HBV cohort; Wong 2013 meta-analysis). Primary non-response or viral breakthrough (≥1-log rise on therapy) prompts adherence review, resistance testing, and regimen change (rare with ETV/TAF/TDF — high genetic barrier). ESCAT IIIA — biomarker directs antiviral continuation/switch decisions and is the primary HCC-prevention lever in chronic HBV.
Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral: Quantitative HBV DNA used to TRACK viral suppression over time during chronic-HBV antiviral therapy (entecavir or tenofovir TDF/TAF — first- line nucleos(t)ide analogues per AASLD 2024 / EASL 2025). Distinct from BIO-HBV-STATUS (serology-based screening / treatment-decision gate). Two clinical contexts: (1) Treatment monitoring in HBeAg+/HBeAg− chronic HBV: baseline HBV DNA + ALT + HBeAg + HBsAg → start NA → recheck q3 months for first year, then q6 months. Goal: HBV DNA undetectable on treatment; ALT normalization; HBeAg seroconversion (HBeAg+ patients) or HBsAg loss (functional cure — rare on NA monotherapy, ~1% per year). Virologic breakthrough (≥1-log rise from nadir) prompts adherence review then switch (entecavir → tenofovir if NA-naïve resistance). (2) Prophylaxis monitoring during B-cell-depleting therapy (rituximab, obinutuzumab) or anti-CD38 (daratumumab, isatuximab) in HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ patients: entecavir prophylaxis baseline → HBV DNA q3 months during chemotherapy and for 12+ months post-treatment; any detectable HBV DNA = reactivation, hepatology consult. AASLD-IDSA / EASL minimum testing protocol: baseline HCV RNA + genotype + cirrhosis staging; on-treatment HCV RNA at week 4 (optional, evaluates adherence/response — undetectable at week 4 = rapid virologic response, RVR; not a stopping rule for modern DAAs); end-of-treatment HCV RNA at completion (week 8 or 12); SVR12 — undetectable HCV RNA 12 weeks after treatment completion = virologic cure (>95% achievable with current DAAs, durable in >99%). SVR12 = primary efficacy endpoint for HCV cure; SVR24 essentially equivalent. Post-SVR HCC surveillance remains REQUIRED in cirrhotic patients (cumulative HCC risk reduced but not eliminated by cure; AASLD recommends ongoing q6-month US ± AFP for cirrhotics regardless of SVR status). R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AM: R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AML (~70-80% of IDH2-mut AML; ~6-8% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved Aug 2017 for R/R-AML-IDH2 monotherapy (phase 1/2: ORR 38%, CR 19%). 1L combination with azacitidine in unfit patients (AG221-AML-005: ORR 71%). Differentiation syndrome (~14%) — same monitoring + dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade; UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML: R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML (~20-30% of IDH2-mut AML; ~2-3% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved across both R140 and R172 variants. Some series (Stein et al., Blood 2017) suggest R172K carries lower CR rate than R140Q on enasidenib mono, but still substantial activity. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) and hyperbilirubinemia same as R140Q. Glioma IDH2 R172K is a separate clinical entity (vorasidenib INDIGO trial) — this biomarker is AML-scoped; glioma IDH2 captured under BIO-IDH-MUTATION composite. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Las alteraciones RB1 (suelción, mutación) ocurren en ~30% del cáncer de vejiga invasivo muscular (MIBC) y se enriquecen en el subtipo molecular basal/escuámico diferenciado (~50%). La pérdida RB1, se asocia con resistencia a los inhibidores CDK4/6 (que requieren pRb para ejercer el arresto G1). En el cáncer urotelial, los inhibidores CDK4/6 son investigadores (no hay indicación aprobada); sin embargo, se está evaluando el estado de RB1 como biomarcador predictivo para la no respuesta de inhibidores de CDK4/6 en cánceres de HR+ en los que los pacientes de vejiga están incluidos en ensayos de cesta. RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.
RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (: RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (pRb), the master G1/S checkpoint regulator. pRb normally sequesters E2F transcription factors to prevent S-phase entry; loss of pRb → uncontrolled cell cycle progression. Clinical contexts: (1) Hereditary retinoblastoma: germline RB1 mutation → bilateral/multifocal retinoblastoma in childhood; lifetime elevated risk of osteosarcoma, SCLC, melanoma. (2) SCLC: biallelic RB1 loss + TP53 mutation defines the SCLC molecular signature (~95% of SCLC). pRb loss by IHC is used in pathologic diagnosis. No targeted therapy for RB1 deficiency per se; SCLC treatment is chemotherapy (EP/EC) ± atezolizumab. (3) Urothelial carcinoma: RB1 alterations in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer; associated with basal/squamous subtype; not currently targeted. (4) Breast cancer: RB1 mutations occur in ~10% of TNBC; RB1 loss predicts resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) — pRb is the substrate for CDK4/6 that drives cell cycle entry; without pRb, CDK4/6 inhibition is ineffective. Las variantes patogénicas de la línea germinal RB1 causan retinoblastoma hereditario (~40% de los casos de retinoblastoma) —enfermedad bilateral / multifocal en 80% de los portadores, edad mediana al diagnóstico ~12 meses. Los portadores enfrentan un riesgo de vida de ~50% de cáncer primario secundario (osteosarcoma, sarcoma de tejido blando, melanoma, pulmón, vejiga); riesgo acumulativo notablemente elevado después de la radioterapia de haz externo (EBRT) — protocolos modernos evitan EBRT para mitigar. Protocolo de vigilancia confirmada (por COG / Grupo Oncológico Infantil + Consorcio Internacional de Retinoblastoma): oftalmología pediátrica con UCE (examen bajo anestesia) que comienza en el período recién nacido — cada 2-4 semanas hasta la edad 1, luego alargamiento progresivo a mensual → q3mo → q6mo hasta la idade 7, anual hasta la adolescencia. Pruebas de cascada a todos los familiares de primer grado obligatorio. Vigilancia de cáncer secundario durante toda la vida: examen anual de la piel, atención al dolor óseo (osteosarcoma en la adolescencia/adulte juvenil), evitación de la radiación ionizante diagnóstica innecesaria. ESCAT IIA.

RET proto-oncogene activating mutation (somatic or germline) in advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC). RET mutations are the defining oncogenic driver of hereditary and sporadic MTC: approximately 25% of sporadic MTC carry somatic RET mutations (M918T in ~50% of these), and hereditary MTC (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A/2B, Familial MTC) is driven by germline RET mutations (C634R/W/Y/F in MEN2A; M918T in MEN2B; C611/C620/C630 in FMTC-risk MEN2A kindreds). Total prevalence of RET-mutant MTC: approximately 60-70% when germline + somatic are combined. RET-mutant status is the primary biomarker gate for selpercatinib over cabozantinib/vandetanib as 1L systemic therapy. LIBRETTO-531 (Wirth NEJM 2024, PMID 39133858) demonstrated selpercatinib superior to physician's choice (cabozantinib or vandetanib) in 1L advanced RET-mutant MTC: median PFS not reached vs 16.8 month...

RET-targeted therapy is typically multi-: RET-targeted therapy is typically multi-year (median PFS >25 mo on selpercatinib in LIBRETTO-001) — chronic exposure raises HBV reactivation risk meaningfully even in HBsAg-negative / anti-HBc+ patients. Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose d: Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the MAIA control arm (Facon NEJM 2019, PMID 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible NDMM. MAIA control arm outcomes: ORR 75.8%, PFS HR (D-Rd vs Rd) 0.56 (95% CI 0.43–0.73), 30-month PFS ~53.3% for D-Rd vs ~37.8% for Rd. Rd continuous showed superiority over MPT and melphalan-prednisone in the FIRST trial (Benboubker NEJM 2014, PMID 25184863): PFS 26 months vs 21.9 months for MPT. Dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "Ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ECOG E4A03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in NDMM (Rajkumar LANCET ONCOL 2010). Renal adjustment is critical: lenalidomide is ~80% renally cleared. CrCl 30-60 → 10 mg daily; CrCl <30 → 5 mg daily or 10 mg qod. Myeloma renal impairment often improves with therapy — recheck CrCl monthly and escalate dose when GFR recovers. Second primary malignancy (SPM) risk: CALGB 100104 and IFM 2005-02 documented elevated SPM (MDS/AML) with lenalidomide maintenance post-ASCT; risk applies to continuous Rd as well at smaller magnitude. Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV: Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV vaccine. Each dose contains virus-like particles (VLPs) assembled from the L1 major capsid protein of two HPV types — 16 and 18 — produced in a baculovirus expression system in Trichoplusia ni insect cells (Hi-5) and adjuvanted with AS04 (3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A on aluminium hydroxide), a TLR4 agonist designed to enhance and prolong the antibody response. L1 VLPs contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG against HPV 16 and 18; cross- neutralization against types 31, 33, 45, 58 is documented (modest efficacy, lower than direct protection). Cancer-prevention pathway: prevents persistent infection with HPV 16 and 18 — responsible for ~70% of cervical cancers, ~80% of anal cancers, ~85% of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers globally. Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent H: Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent HPV vaccine. Each dose contains virus-like particles (VLPs) assembled from the L1 major capsid protein of nine HPV types — 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58 — produced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and adjuvanted with amorphous aluminium hydroxyphosphate sulfate (AAHS). L1 VLPs are immunogenic but contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG that prevents incident infection by the covered HPV types. Cancer-prevention pathway: prevents persistent infection with the HPV types responsible for ~90% of cervical cancers, ~90% of anal cancers, ~70% of vaginal/vulvar cancers, ~60% of penile cancers, and a growing fraction of oropharyngeal cancers.
Recombinant non-infectious vaccine conta: Recombinant non-infectious vaccine containing hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) produced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Engerix-B, Recombivax HB) or in mammalian cells (PreHevbrio — tri-antigen S/preS1/ preS2). HBsAg contains no viral DNA — cannot cause HBV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer anti-HBs neutralizing IgG that prevents incident HBV infection on exposure. CANCER-PREVENTION PATHWAY: chronic HBV infection is responsible for ~50% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) globally and a subset of HBV-associated B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas; preventing chronic HBV via vaccination is the single most effective primary- prevention intervention for HCC (WHO + IARC).

La monografía IARC 116 (2016) clasificó el consumo de bebidas muy calientes a más de 65°C como Grupo 2A (probablemente cancerígeno) — evidencia limitada en humanos (asociaciones consistentes con carcinoma escamoso de células esofágicas en cohortes de beber mate, té caliente y café caliente, con confusión residual de la coexposición tabaco/alcool no totalmente excluida), evidencia suficiente en animales experimentales (lesión térmica → inflamación crónica → carcinogénesis de campo en modelos de esófago de roedores). Regular consumption of very hot beverage: Regular consumption of very hot beverages (≥65°C / 149°F) per IARC Monograph 116 (2016) — applies primarily to teas (especially traditional preparation styles in regions of Iran, Turkey, China, parts of South America with maté), but also coffee/water consumed at scalding temperatures. IARC Group 2A (probably carcinogenic) classification — associated with esophageal squamous-cell carcinoma (ESCC), particularly in regions with high background ESCC incidence. Mechanism: thermal injury to esophageal epithelium → chronic inflammation → field carcinogenesis. Note: at typical Western coffee/tea temperatures (<60°C), no association observed; coffee + tea per se are not carcinogenic. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g: Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g/day per WCRF/IARC threshold. IARC Monograph 114 (2015) classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogen for colorectal cancer (sufficient evidence). Each 50 g/day of processed meat increases CRC risk by ~18% (meta-analyzed RR ~1.18; WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating). Processed meat = sausages, ham, bacon, salami, cured/smoked/salted/preserved meat. Red meat (Group 2A per IARC, probable carcinogen) is a separate but overlapping concern — threshold ≥500 g/week for red meat. Mechanisms: N-nitroso compounds, heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heme iron. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Relapsed/refractory DLBCL with confirmed CD20 expression on malignant B-cells, post ≥2 prior systemic therapies including one anti-CD20 antibody-containing regimen (R-CHOP), CAR-T-ineligible or post-CAR-T failure — candidate for epcoritamab (CD20xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager; subcutaneous step-up administration). Pivotal data EPCORE NHL-1 phase 1/2 (Thieblemont 2023 J Clin Oncol): ORR 63%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.4 mo, mDOR 12 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T for non-eligible / bridging / post-failure setting. Distinct from glofitamab (different schedule: fixed 12 cycles vs continuous; IV vs SC). CD20-loss escape post-prior-anti-CD20 is a documented mechanism — re-biopsy advisable for late-relapse cohorts.

Reproductive history combining late first full-term pregnancy (age ≥30) OR nulliparity, AND short cumulative lifetime breastfeeding duration (<6 months total). Both factors independently confer modest increases in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer risk (RR ~1.2-1.4 each) per Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer + WCRF/AICR. Effect cumulative with other reproductive factors (early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT). Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive pilot).

Reserve antibiotic — escalation choice i: Reserve antibiotic — escalation choice in febrile neutropenia after 72-96 hours of empirical pip-tazo or cefepime without clinical improvement, and first-line for documented or strongly suspected MDR Gram-negative infection (ESBL Enterobacterales, AmpC overproducers, Pseudomonas with broad resistance). Antimicrobial stewardship critical: prolonged carbapenem use selects for carbapenem-resistant organisms (KPC, NDM, OXA-48). CRITICAL interaction: meropenem dramatically reduces valproate levels (60-100% drop within hours) — patients on valproate for seizures or mood stabilization need a switch to levetiracetam BEFORE meropenem start, with overlap of 2-3 days. Lower seizure risk than imipenem, but still elevated with renal dysfunction and CNS pathology — meticulous renal dosing required. Avoid in uncomplicated indications where pip-tazo or cefepime suffices. Ukraine: widely available, NSZU-covered for critical infections.

Also part of the IMspire150 triplet (atezolizumab + cobimetinib + vemurafenib) for previously untreated BRAF V600 advanced melanoma, where the addition of atezolizumab modestly extended PFS. Revumenib (SNDX-5613), an oral menin inhibitor, is FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia (AML and ALL). AUGMENT-101 (Issa et al. NEJM 2023; Erba et al. ASH 2023 update): KMT2A-rearranged R/R AML/ALL — ORR 23% (CR + CRh + CRi), complete remission with full recovery 18%; mOS 8.0 mo. FDA accelerated approval based on remission rate as surrogate endpoint. KMT2A rearrangement is present in ~10% of adult AML (more common in secondary/therapy-related AML and infant leukemia). Menin is an essential co-factor of KMT2A-fusion oncoproteins — revumenib disrupts menin-MLL interaction, restoring differentiation block. Revumenib (menin inhibitor) FDA-approved (Nov 2024) for relapsed/refractory KMT2A-rearranged acute leukemia including B-ALL. AUGMENT-101 combined KMT2A-rearranged cohort (AML + ALL): ORR 23%, CR/CRh 18%. KMT2A rearrangement defines a high-risk B-ALL subset: in infants KMT2A-AFF1 is present in ~80% of infant B-ALL (EFS <30% with standard chemotherapy); in adults KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL is adverse-risk (NCCN/ELN). Revumenib represents a first targeted option for this historically chemotherapy-refractory population. Blinatumomab (CD19 BiTE, FDA-approved for R/R B-ALL) and inotuzumab ozogamicin are also active in KMT2A-rearranged B-ALL regardless of KMT2A status, but revumenib is the first mutation-specific approved agent. AlloHCT in CR remains the standard consolidation for eligible adults.

Ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) received FD: Ruxolitinib cream (Opzelura) received FDA approval (September 2022) for mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis; separately, ruxolitinib phosphate (Jakafi, oral) is FDA-approved for steroid-refractory acute/chronic GVHD but NOT specifically approved for CTCL as of 2026. However, the JAK/STAT pathway is aberrantly activated in MF/SS (~30–50% have JAK3 mutations or JAK1/STAT3/STAT5 alterations), making JAK inhibitors an active investigational area. Phase II evidence: ruxolitinib (oral) ORR ~29% in relapsed/refractory MF (RUXO-MF pilot data); itacitinib (JAK1 inhibitor) and cerdulatinib (JAK/SYK inhibitor) in phase II trials for CTCL. The CTCL-specific approvals are for non-JAK-targeted agents: romidepsin (HDAC inhibitor; FDA 2009 CTCL), brentuximab vedotin (CD30+; FDA 2017), mogamulizumab (CCR4; FDA 2018), vorinostat (FDA 2006). JAK3-mutant CTCL: JAK3 mutation identifies a subset with stronger a priori rationale for JAK inhibitor use; ESCAT IIA reflects absence of dedicated FDA approval in CTCL despite biological rationale and early phase data.

Aggressive EGFR-class skin care (clindamycin gel, oral doxycycline 100 mg BID prophylaxis, emollients, sun protection); paronychia: chlorhexidine soaks + high-potency topical steroid + careful nail care. SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core sub: SMARCB1 (INI1/hSNF5/BAF47) is a core subunit of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling complex. Biallelic inactivation removes SWI/SNF antagonism of EZH2 (PRC2 complex), leading to H3K27me3 accumulation and epigenetic silencing of tumor suppressor genes. This makes SMARCB1-deficient tumors selectively sensitive to EZH2 inhibition. SMARCB1 loss defines three main tumor types: (1) Epithelioid sarcoma — tazemetostat FDA-approved (2020; EZH-202 trial). (2) Malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT, AT/RT in CNS) — extremely aggressive; no approved targeted therapy; investigational EZH2 inhibitors. (3) SMARCB1-deficient chordoma, sinonasal carcinoma — rare. IHC for INI1 (nuclear loss) is the companion diagnostic for tazemetostat in epithelioid sarcoma and is simpler than molecular testing. Note: retained INI1 expression does NOT exclude epithelioid sarcoma — ~10% of cases have normal INI1 by IHC despite molecular loss (technical or heterogeneous loss).

SMO (Smoothened) is a G-protein-coupled: SMO (Smoothened) is a G-protein-coupled receptor that transmits Hedgehog (HH) signaling. Normally suppressed by PTCH1; activated when PTCH1 loses its inhibitory function (whether via PTCH1 loss-of-function or SMO gain-of-function mutation). SMO activating mutations (~10–20% of BCCs) and PTCH1 loss-of-function (~90% of BCCs) both result in constitutive HH pathway activation. Vismodegib and sonidegib are SMO antagonists — they bind the SMO transmembrane domain and block downstream HH signaling (GLI1/2 repression). In practice, BCC HHI therapy does not require pre-testing for SMO vs PTCH1 mutation — all BCCs have HH pathway activation. SMO mutations also occur in sporadic medulloblastoma (SHH subtype) and rarely in other tumors. Resistance: secondary SMO mutations (D473H most common) emerge during vismodegib therapy, driving acquired resistance. Sonidegib may be active in some vismodegib-resistant D473H mutants.

Not a treatment biomarker — screening-pathway selector only.

SUFU germline pathogenic variants cause a Gorlin-syndrome–like predisposition with much higher medulloblastoma risk than PTCH1 (~30% lifetime vs ~5% in PTCH1), and lower BCC burden. SUFU-driven medulloblastomas cluster in the SHH-activated molecular subgroup (infant/young-child onset, desmoplastic / MBEN histology in many cases). Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per Foulkes et al. 2017 / AACR Pediatric Predisposition Working Group): brain MRI q4mo from diagnosis through age 3, q6mo from age 3-5, annually to age 8 — denser-than-PTCH1 cadence reflects higher MB risk. Dermatology surveillance for BCC q6-12mo from puberty. Avoid craniospinal external-beam radiation when alternatives exist (second-malignancy risk in carriers). Hedgehog-pathway inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) have limited activity in SUFU-mutant SHH-MB — downstream-of-SMO position renders SMO inhibitors ineffective; this is a critical distinction from PTCH1-driven disease. ESCAT IIA.
SUFU germline — drives Gorlin-syndrome v: SUFU germline — drives Gorlin-syndrome variant with markedly higher pediatric medulloblastoma risk (~33%, SHH-subtype, often <3 years) compared with PTCH1-Gorlin (~5%). Lower BCC burden than PTCH1. Other features overlap NBCCS (jaw keratocysts may be less prevalent). AVOID craniospinal radiation when feasible — drives second primaries / treatment-related BCCs. Surveillance: brain MRI every 3-4 months in infants/young children. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.
SUNLIGHT trial (Prager 2023): 3L+ mCRC a: Ensayo SUNLIGHT (Prager 2023): 3L+ mCRC después de la quimioterapia estándar — TAS-102 + bevacizumab vs TAS102 solo mejoró mOS 10,8 vs 7,5 mo (HR 0,61), PFS 5,6 vs 2,4 mo (RR 0,44), ORR 6,3% vs 1,0%. La combinación es ahora la opción preferida de 3L + por NCCN 2025. Mecanismo distinto de la exposición previa a la fluoropirimidina (incorporación analógica de TS-independente, timidina) — activa en enfermedad refractaria 5-FU. Reacciones de los pies notablemente menores que la furopirimidina; toxicidad principal es mielosupresión.

Screening-context entry for PSA — separa: Screening-context entry for PSA — separate from BIO-PSA (which covers diagnostic and treatment-monitoring dynamics for established prostate cancer). USPSTF 2018: Grade C for men 55-69 (individualized shared-decision-making about benefits + harms); Grade D for men ≥70 (recommend AGAINST routine screening). NCCN 2025 (Early Detection): baseline PSA + DRE discussion at age 45 for African American men or BRCA2 carriers (high-risk groups), age 50 for average risk; if PSA <1 ng/mL, repeat every 2-4 years; if PSA 1-3 ng/mL, repeat every 1-2 years; if PSA >3 ng/mL, evaluate further (repeat PSA, mpMRI, biomarker reflex such as 4Kscore/PHI, possible biopsy). Higher screening intensity for confirmed BRCA2 germline carriers (IMPACT study — PSA q1y starting age 40; biopsy threshold ≥3 ng/mL). PSA can be falsely elevated in BPH, prostatitis, urinary retention, recent instrumentation. Free PSA ratio, PSA density, and reflex biomarkers (PHI, 4Kscore, SelectMDx) reduce unnecessary biopsy. Limitations: overdiagnosis/overtreatment of indolent cancers (well-characterized harm — driver of USPSTF Grade C). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Second most common IDH1 variant. Distrib: Second most common IDH1 variant. Distribution differs by disease: R132C is the dominant IDH1 variant in cholangiocarcinoma (~25-30% of IDH1-mutant CCA per ClarIDHy) and chondrosarcoma; in glioma it is rarer than R132H (<5%); in AML R132C accounts for ~30% of IDH1 mutations. Critically, R132C is IHC-NEGATIVE with the R132H-specific antibody (clone H09) — relying on IHC alone misses these patients. Ivosidenib (Tibsovo) is approved for IDH1-mutant cholangiocarcinoma (ClarIDHy 2L+) and IDH1-mutant AML (AGILE in combination with azacitidine 1L unfit; monotherapy R/R) — labels cover all IDH1 variants on the proven hotspot list (R132C/R132G/R132H/R132L/R132S), not just R132H. Reuses existing REG-IVOSIDENIB and IDH1-keyed indications via this biomarker entity.
Second of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder: Second of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations. Single-nucleotide duplication (cytosine) in exon 20 causing frameshift and premature termination — truncates BRCA1 within the BRCT2 domain, abolishing C-terminal protein-binding function critical for homologous-recombination repair coordination. Also called 5382insC in legacy nomenclature (offset by stop-codon counting convention shift). Recurrent founder effect in AJ populations (~0.8-1.0% carrier frequency in AJ vs <0.1% non-AJ); also reported as a recurrent variant in Polish, Russian, Belarusian populations (likely separate founder events or AJ admixture). Lifetime cancer risks consistent with BRCA1 average. NCCN 2025 endorses population-wide AJ founder-panel testing (3-mutation panel) regardless of family history. Same surveillance and risk-reduction protocols as other BRCA1 pathogenic variants. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

Second-generation HIV-1 integrase strand: Second-generation HIV-1 integrase strand-transfer inhibitor (INSTI) formulated as a long-acting injectable nanosuspension. Blocks integration of viral DNA into the host chromosome — same INSTI mechanism as dolutegravir and bictegravir, with similar high barrier to resistance. Sustained-release IM depot provides therapeutic plasma cabotegravir for ~2-3 months per dose. As HIV-1 PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS in HIV-negative adults at substantial risk, CAB-LA reduces sexual HIV acquisition by ~69% vs daily oral FTC/TDF in HPTN 083 (cisgender MSM / transgender women) and by ~89% in HPTN 084 (cisgender women at risk in sub-Saharan Africa) — superior efficacy to oral PrEP, driven by improved adherence over daily pills. Second-generation phosphonamidate prodru: Fosfonamido de segunda generación prodroga de tenofovir; estabilizado para resistir la hidrólisis plasmática (versus TDF) por lo que entrega preferentemente tenofrovir intracelular a hepatocitos (HBV) y linfocitos(VIH). Una vez en célula diana, la catepsina intracelular A se clava TAF a tenoforovir, que luego se fosforila a tenosovir-DP y inhibe competitivamente la polimerasa HBV / VIH-1 trascrinxasa inversa con terminación de cadena. Rendimiento ~90% menor exposición sistémica al tenofovir que el TDF a concentraciones intracelulares equivalentes, menor toxicidad renal y ósea.
