Secondary-amine tricyclic antidepressant: Antidepresivos tricíclicos de la amina secundaria; la acción primaria es la inhibición de la recaptación de noradrenalina (inhibición moderada de la recaptación de serotonina), con antagonismo en los receptores histamínicos H1, muscarínico y α1-adrenérgico. El mecanismo de cesación del tabaco no está plenamente establecido; las contribuciones propuestas incluyen la modulación noradrenérgica de la abstinencia de la nicotina, la mitigación de la ansiedad/síntomos depresivos durante los intentos de cesar y el efecto directo en los circuitos dopaminérgicos relacionados con el tabaquismo. Metaanálisis de cochrane (actualización de Hughes 2014) — la nortriptilina aproximadamente duplica las tasas de cese a largo plazo frente a placebo (RR ~2,0), comparable a bupropión y TRN; menor evidencia y tolerancia más baja que la vareniclina (DRUG-VARENICLINE — primera línea por USPSTF 2021). Uso de lavabo off; segunda / tercera línea opción para cesar cuando varenicina / bupropion / TRN han fallado o están contraindicados.
Select persistent, unexplained, or new f: Seleccione hallazgos persistentes, inexplicables o nuevos.
Selective 5-HT3 receptor antagonist; blo: Antagónico selectivo de los receptores 5-HT3; bloquea la estimulación vagal del reflejo de vómitos.
Selective ATP-competitive BRAF V600E/K k: Selective ATP-competitive BRAF V600E/K kinase inhibitor. Longer target-residence time vs vemurafenib/dabrafenib → less paradoxical ERK activation in WT BRAF cells. In mCRC BRAF V600E + cetuximab (BEACON CRC) — first BRAF-targeted approval in CRC.
Selective ATP-competitive small-molecule: Selective ATP-competitive small-molecule TKI of VEGFR-1, VEGFR-2, and VEGFR-3 with sub-nanomolar in-vitro potency and improved selectivity over first-generation multikinase TKIs (sunitinib, sorafenib). Blocks VEGF-driven endothelial proliferation, migration, and survival in the tumor microenvironment, producing predominantly anti-angiogenic effects with minimal direct cytotoxicity. Short half-life (~2.5-6 h) gives titratable BID dosing — characteristic patient-specific dose escalation based on blood-pressure response (titrate up to 10 mg BID if BP tolerable at 5 mg). Pivotal evidence: AXIS (axitinib vs sorafenib 2L mRCC post-sunitinib/cytokines: mPFS 6.7 vs 4.7 mo); KEYNOTE-426 (pembrolizumab + axitinib vs sunitinib 1L mRCC: mPFS 15.7 vs 11.1 mo, OS HR 0.53), JAVELIN Renal 101 (avelumab + axitinib vs sunitinib 1L mRCC).
Selective BCL-2 inhibitor (BH3 mimetic): Inhibidor selectivo de la BCL-2 (mimético BH3)
Selective BRAF V600E/K inhibitor. Always: Inhibidor selectivo de BRAF V600E/K. Siempre combinado con trametinib (MEKi) para prevenir la activación paradójica de RAF en las células BRAF-WT y mejorar la eficacia.
Selective Coverage Versus Comprehensive: Cobertura selectiva contra cobertura integral Radioterapia en cáncer de tiroides mal diferenciado y anaplásico
Selective FLT3 + AXL tyrosine kinase inh: Inhibidor selectivo de la FLT3 + AXL de tirosina quinasa (tipo I)
Selective IDH1 inhibitor for R/R IDH1-mu: Selective IDH1 inhibitor for R/R IDH1-mutant AML in adults. Pivotal Study 2102-HEM-101 (single-arm, n=153, R/R IDH1-mut AML, olutasidenib 150 mg PO BID) — CR + CRh 35%; mDOR 25.9 mo (CR/CRh subgroup); transfusion independence 56-month; ~30% transitioned to allo-HSCT. Compares favorably to ivosidenib (alternative IDH1 inhibitor — separate regimen entity, future). BOXED WARNINGS: differentiation syndrome (~16%) + hepatotoxicity (~21% Grade ≥3 transaminitis). Used as bridge to allo-HSCT in fit patients. Ivosidenib + azacitidine combination (AGILE trial, newly-diagnosed unfit IDH1-mut AML) is a separate regimen entity. STUB — pending Study 2102-HEM-101 trial Source ingestion (SRC-OLUTASIDENIB-DEBOTTON-2023) and Co-Lead sign-off.
Selective IDH2 (mutant) enzyme inhibitor: Inhibidor selectivo de la enzima IDH2 (mutante)
Selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor. Blocks JA: Selective JAK1/JAK2 inhibitor. Blocks JAK-STAT signaling driven by JAK2 V617F (and CALR/MPL via JAK2 dimerization). Reduces splenomegaly + symptoms in MF/PV/ET; does not eliminate clone. Backbone of MF symptom-driven therapy.
Selective JAK2 inhibitor for MF post-rux: Inhibidor selectivo de JAK2 para la insuficiencia o intolerancia post-ruxolitinib de MF. JAQARTA-2 fase-2 + confirmación de fase 3 de LIBERTAD-2. Alerta en el encefalopatía de Wernicke — medición obligatoria de tiamina + suplementación. Tomar con alimentos. STUB — pendiente de firma de Co-Lead.
Selective JAK2 inhibitor with FLT3 activ: Inhibidor selectivo de JAK2 con actividad FLT3. Activo en MF después de fallo / intolerancia de ruxolitinib. Advertencia en caja para encefalopatía de Wernicke (deficiencia de tiamina).
Selective KIT and PDGFRA inhibitor desig: Inhibidor selectivo del KIT y del PDGFRA diseñado para unir la conformación activa; activo exclusivamente contra el KIT resistente al imatinib D816V (mastocitosis sistémica avanzada) y las mutaciones activadoras del PDFFRA D842V (GIST). NAVIGATOR (PDGFRAD842 V GIST) ORR ~88%; EXPLORER + PATHFINDER (SM avanzada) Orro ~75% con respuestas moleculares profundas.
Selective MEK inhibitor used in combinat: Inhibidor selectivo MEK utilizado en combinación con dabrafenib. Reduce la resistencia + toxicidad cutánea vs. BRAFi solo.
Selective MET inhibitor with similar eff: Inhibidor selectivo del MET con perfil de eficacia similar al de capmatinib. Ensayo VISION: ORR ~46% en 1L MET ex14+ NSCLC.
Selective RET tyrosine kinase inhibitor: Inhibidor selectivo de la tirosina quinasa RET
Selective RNA polymerase II inhibitor (a: Selective RNA polymerase II inhibitor (alkylating-like trabectedin analogue)
Selective TKI of BCR-ABL1 (~30× more pot: Selective TKI of BCR-ABL1 (~30× more potent than imatinib). Active against most imatinib-resistant mutations except T315I, V299L, F317L. Vascular adverse-event profile (PAOD, MI, stroke) is the dose-limiting concern long-term.
Selective TKI of BCR-ABL1, KIT, PDGFR-α/: Selective TKI of BCR-ABL1, KIT, PDGFR-α/β. Founder of the targeted CML era. Standard CML 1L for low-risk, comorbid, or cost-constrained patients.
Selective VEGFR-1/2/3 tyrosine kinase in: Inhibidor selectivo de VEGFR-1/2/3 de tirosina quinasa (2a generación)
Selective allosteric (non-ATP-competitiv: Selective allosteric (non-ATP-competitive) inhibitor of MEK1/MEK2 kinases that bind a pocket adjacent to the ATP site, locking MEK in an inactive conformation. Blocks downstream phosphorylation of ERK1/2 in the constitutively activated RAS/RAF/MEK/ERK pathway, suppressing proliferation and survival signaling in BRAF V600-mutant tumor cells. Combined with a BRAF inhibitor (encorafenib) the doublet mitigates paradoxical MAPK reactivation seen with BRAFi monotherapy and prolongs response duration. Clinical evidence: COLUMBUS (encorafenib + binimetinib vs vemurafenib in BRAF V600 unresectable / metastatic melanoma, mPFS 14.9 vs 7.3 mo, mOS 33.6 vs 16.9 mo). Historically evaluated as the third agent in BEACON-CRC triplet (no OS gain over encorafenib + cetuximab doublet — doublet is the standard for BRAF V600E mCRC).
Selective alpha-1 blockade gives less re: Selective alpha-1 blockade gives less reflex tachycardia and easier general availability than phenoxybenzamine (DRUG-PHENOXYBENZAMINE), making doxazosin a commonly used practical alternative for mandatory preoperative PPGL alpha-blockade; choice between the two is per local practice/availability, not modelled as a KB-level preference. STUB pending clinical co-lead signoff (CHARTER §6.1, dev-mode-exempted).
Selective competitive antagonist at the: Antagónico competitivo selectivo en el receptor de serotonina de 5-hidroxitriptamina tipo 3 (5-HT3) situado periféricamente en las terminales vagales aferentes en el tracto GI y centralmente en la zona de desencadenamiento del receptor quimio (zona postrema). Características diferenciales vs antagonistas de primera generación 5-HT3 (ondansetron, granisetron): afinidad de unión de los receptores ~30× más alta, ~7× semivida plasmática más larga (~40 h vs ~4-6 h), y demostró interacciones cruzadas de receptor alostérico con receptores NK1 que contribuyen a un control superior de la NVCI de fase retrasada. Una dosis única IV o oral cubre tanto las fases agudas (0-24 h) como retrasadas (24-120 h) de la VCI. Aprobado por la FDA julio de 2003 y EMA marzo 2005.

Selective competitive antagonist at the histamine H2 receptor on gastric parietal cells, blocking histamine-stimulated gastric acid secretion (basal, nocturnal, food-stimulated, and pentagastrin- stimulated) — produces ~50-90% acid suppression depending on dose. In allergic reactions and chemotherapy infusion reactions, the H2 antagonism complements H1 antagonist (diphenhydramine) blockade — histamine acts on both H1 (bronchospasm, vasodilation, urticaria, pruritus) AND H2 (vasodilation, gastric secretion, cardiac inotropy) receptors, and combined H1 + H2 blockade is superior to either alone for prevention and treatment of urticaria, mild anaphylactoid reactions, and chemotherapy infusion reactions (paclitaxel, carboplatin retreatment, monoclonal antibodies). Famotidine is preferred among H2 antagonists in oncology because of lack of CYP-mediated drug interactions (cimetidine inhibits C...
Selective competitive antagonist of the: Antagónico competitivo selectivo de la sustancia receptor P / NK1 en los centros eméticos del SNC (nucleus tractus solitarius, área postrema), bloqueando la fase tardía de náuseas y vómitos (NVCI) inducidas por quimioterapia mediados por la sustancia P. La característica farmacocinética distintiva es una semivida terminal excepcionalmente larga de ~7 días (~169 horas), que proporciona cobertura del receptor durante la fase completa de retraso de 5 días a partir de una única dosis oral sin necesidad de dosis de seguimiento en los días 2-3. Aprobado por la FDA septiembre 2015 y EMA abril 2017 para la prevención de retraso de CINV en adultos que reciben HEC o MEC.
Selective estrogen receptor degrader (SE: Degradador selectivo del receptor de estrógeno (SERD) — contexto de quimioprevención únicamente para investigación
Selective estrogen receptor modulator (S: Modulador selectivo del receptor de estrógeno (SERM)
Selective high-affinity antagonist of th: Selective high-affinity antagonist of the human substance P / neurokinin-1 (NK1) receptor in the central nervous system, blocking the late vomiting signal mediated by substance P binding in the nucleus tractus solitarius and area postrema. This complements the early-phase blockade by 5-HT3 antagonists (which control acute CINV) by preventing the delayed phase (24-120 h post-chemotherapy). Standard component of triple-antiemetic prophylaxis (NK1 + 5-HT3 + dexamethasone, ± olanzapine) for highly emetogenic chemotherapy (HEC) such as cisplatin ≥50 mg/m², AC (anthracycline + cyclophosphamide), and BEACOPP. Approved by FDA March 2003 and EMA November 2003.
Selective inhibitor of MET (c-MET) tyros: Selective inhibitor of MET (c-MET) tyrosine kinase. GEOMETRY mono-1: ORR ~68% in 1L MET ex14-mutant NSCLC.
Selective inhibitor of PI3K-alpha (p110α: Selective inhibitor of PI3K-alpha (p110α isoform). Active in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- metastatic — combined with fulvestrant per SOLAR-1.
Selective inhibitor of cyclin-dependent: Inhibidor selectivo de las cinasas 4 y 6 dependientes de la cicloína — bloques de la fosforilación Rb, bloqueo de las células en G1. Combinado con el tratamiento endocrino en HR+/HER2- metastásico; beneficio adyuvante modesto (PALLAS / PENELOPE-B negativo).
Selective inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-2: Selective inhibitor of cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2; ~10-20-fold selectivity over COX-1 at therapeutic concentrations), suppressing prostaglandin- driven inflammation, proliferation, and angiogenesis with relatively spared platelet COX-1 (no antiplatelet effect at standard doses) and reduced gastric mucosal COX-1 (less GI bleeding than non-selective NSAIDs). Cancer-prevention rationale: COX-2 is upregulated in adenomas and many tumors; inhibition reduces PGE2-driven proliferation and immune escape. In FAP, celecoxib reduced duodenal polyp burden (Steinbach NEJM 2000) — formerly FDA-approved for FAP-related polyposis (orphan designation), withdrawn 2011 by sponsor after post-marketing study did not confirm benefit.
Selective irreversible (covalent) FGFR1/: Inhibidor selectivo de tirosina quinasa (covalente) FGFR1/2/3//4
Selective irreversible CYP17A1 inhibitor: Inhibidor selectivo irreversible del CYP17A1 — bloquea la síntesis de androgénios suprarrenais e intratumorales (testosterona, precursores de DHT) siempre combinado con corticosteroides de dosis baja (prednisona) para mitigar el exceso mineralocorticoide (hipertensión, hipokalemia, retención de líquidos).
Selective irreversible inhibitor of the: Inhibidor selectivo irreversible de la actividad similar a la quimotripsina de la 20S proteasoma (subunidades β5 / LMP7). Ata covalentemente a través de epoxicetona —distinta de la unión reversible del boronato de bortezomib — que confiere inhibición sostenida + actividad en mieloma refratario de bortézomibe. Dosis únicas pueden suprimir la actividad proteasomática >80% durante >24h.
Selective menin-MLL (KMT2A) interaction: Inhibidor selectivo de la interacción de la menina-MLL (KMT2A)
Selective oral FGFR1/2/3 tyrosine kinase: Inhibidor de tirosina quinasa selectivo por vía oral FGFR1/2/3
Selective oral inhibitor of CSF1R (colon: Selective oral inhibitor of CSF1R (colony-stimulating factor 1 receptor), KIT, and FLT3. In TGCT (formerly PVNS), tumor cells overexpress CSF1 (via COL6A3-CSF1 translocation), driving recruitment of CSF1R-expressing macrophages and osteoclast-like giant cells that constitute the bulk of the tumor mass. Pexidartinib depletes these CSF1R+ cells, reducing tumor burden. ILLUMINATE trial: ORR 38% (vs 0% placebo), with 15% complete response. FDA-approved August 2019 — first systemic therapy for TGCT.
Selective oral inhibitor of EZH2 (Enhanc: Inhibidor oral selectivo de EZH2 (Enhancer de Zeste Homolog 2) — la subunidad catalítica de PRC2 (Complexo Repressivo de Polycomb 2). Bloquea la trimetilación H3K27, desreprimiendo los genes supresores de tumores. Efectivo contra tanto el tipo salvaje EZh2 (dependiencia epigenética) como el aumento de función del Y641 mutado FL — respuesta superior en subconjunto mutado.
Selective oral mutant IDH1 (R132) inhibi: Inhibidor selectivo del mutante oral IDH1 (R132)
Selective partial agonist at the α4β2 ni: Agonista parcial selectivo en el receptor de acetilcolina α4β2 nicotínica, el principal mediador de la recompensa dopaminérgica inducida por la nicotina. El agonismo parcial produce una modesta liberación de dopamina (aliviando el antojo y la abstinencia) mientras bloquea simultáneamente la unión de la nicatina (reduciendo el refuerzo de los cigarrillos fumados durante la titulación).
Selective retinoid X receptor (RXR) agon: Agonista selectivo del receptor X retinoide (RXR)
Selective short-acting β2-adrenergic ago: Selective short-acting β2-adrenergic agonist that activates β2 receptors on bronchial smooth muscle, stimulating adenylyl cyclase → increased intracellular cAMP → relaxation of bronchial smooth muscle and bronchodilation. Onset of action 5-15 min after inhalation, peak effect 30-60 min, duration 4-6 h. Also produces mast cell membrane stabilization (modestly reducing histamine release), enhanced mucociliary clearance, and decreased microvascular permeability. Selectivity for β2 over β1 (~30:1) limits cardiac stimulation at therapeutic doses but loses selectivity at high doses or with parenteral routes (tachycardia, palpitations, modest blood pressure changes). In oncology supportive care, used for: (1) bronchospasm component of chemotherapy infusion reactions and anaphylaxis (adjunct to epinephrine, NOT substitute); (2) acute exacerbations of underlying asthma / COPD precipitated by inf...
Selective small-molecule inhibitor of hy: Selective small-molecule inhibitor of hypoxia-inducible factor 2α (HIF-2α). VHL inactivation (somatic in ~90% of clear-cell RCC, germline in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome) → HIF-2α stabilization → drives the angiogenic/glycolytic ccRCC phenotype. Belzutifan disrupts HIF-2α heterodimerization with HIF-1β, suppressing the downstream transcriptional programme.
Selective, competitive alpha-1 adrenergi: Antagónico selectivo y competitivo de los receptores adrenérgicos alfa-1
Selective, high-affinity D2-dopamine rec: Selective, high-affinity D2-dopamine receptor agonist with a long elimination half-life (~65 hours) permitting once- or twice-weekly oral dosing. Activates D2 receptors on pituitary lactotroph cells, suppressing prolactin synthesis/secretion and inducing lactotroph adenoma shrinkage in the majority of prolactinomas. First-line therapy for prolactinoma; superior prolactin-normalization rate, tumor-shrinkage rate, and tolerability compared with bromocriptine (older, less selective dopamine agonist).
Selectively and reversibly blocks post-s: Selectively and reversibly blocks post-synaptic alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, reducing catecholamine-mediated peripheral vasoconstriction with less reflex tachycardia than non-selective irreversible agents (phenoxybenzamine) because alpha-2 presynaptic auto-inhibition of norepinephrine release is preserved. Used as an alternative preoperative alpha-blocker in pheochromocytoma / paraganglioma (PPGL) where mandatory preoperative alpha-blockade is required before surgery to prevent intraoperative hypertensive crisis (Endocrine Society 2014 PPGL guideline).
Selectively binds BCL-2, displaces pro-a: Selectively binds BCL-2, displaces pro-apoptotic BH3 proteins, restores apoptosis in BCL-2-dependent cancer cells. Highly active in CLL (where CLL is BCL-2-addicted), AML, multiple myeloma. Substantial tumor lysis risk at initiation — strict 5-week dose ramp + TLS prophylaxis required.
Selectively binds and activates retinoid: Selectively binds and activates retinoid X receptors (RXRα, RXRβ, RXRγ), which heterodimerize with other nuclear receptors to regulate gene expression involved in cellular differentiation and proliferation. In CTCL induces apoptosis and differentiation of malignant T-cells.
Selectively phosphorylated by viral thym: Selectively phosphorylated by viral thymidine kinase to acyclovir monophosphate, then by host kinases to acyclovir triphosphate, which inhibits viral DNA polymerase and terminates viral DNA chain elongation. Active against HSV-1, HSV-2, VZV; modest activity against EBV, CMV.
Selectively reduces platelet count by in: Reduce selectivamente el recuento de plaquetas interfiriendo con la diferenciación de megacariocitos. No disminuye la CBC o Hct (a diferencia de HU). Usado como citoreducción de 2L en ET cuando HU es intolerado o insuficiente.

Serum AFP is used in combination with ultrasound every 6 months for HCC surveillance in cirrhotic patients of any aetiology (Child-Pugh A/B7, candidates for treatment) and in non-cirrhotic chronic HBV with elevated HCC risk per AASLD HCC 2023. US-alone sensitivity is suboptimal (~63%); US + AFP raises sensitivity for early-stage HCC to ~70-80% with acceptable specificity (~85-90%). AFP threshold typically >20 ng/mL (some guidelines >7 ng/mL with risk-stratified cutoffs). Rising AFP trajectory is more informative than single value. AFP elevation also occurs in chronic hepatitis flares, regenerative nodules, germ-cell tumours, and gestation — interpret in context. Diagnostic workup of rising AFP: multiphasic CT or MRI per LI-RADS criteria. AFP-L3 fraction and DCP (PIVKA-II) are adjunct markers in some practices. ESCAT IIIA — AFP directs HCC diagnostic workup / surveillance cadence.

Serum calcitonin is a highly specific biomarker for medullary thyroid carcinoma (MTC) — produced by parafollicular C-cells. In MEN2 RET germline carriers, calcitonin trends inform timing of prophylactic thyroidectomy (RET codon-stratified per ATA Thyroid 2015 + Endocrine Society MEN 2023): - MEN2B (M918T): prophylactic thyroidectomy <1 year, before calcitonin rise becomes detectable - MEN2A high-risk codons (634, 883): thyroidectomy by age 5 - MEN2A moderate-risk codons (609, 611, 618, 620, 630, 631): may delay until calcitonin becomes detectable on stimulation testing Basal + stimulated (pentagastrin / calcium-stimulated where available) calcitonin tracks residual disease post-thyroidectomy. CEA is a complementary marker. Doubling time of calcitonin post-resection is a strong prognostic indicator (<6 mo = aggressive). ESCAT IIIA — calcitonin directs prophylactic surgery timing and post-operative monitoring.

Aproximadamente el 30% de los CCRs no secretan CEA (histologías microsatélite-instable, mucíneas, sigilloso-ring); en esos pacientes la vigilancia CEA tiene un rendimiento limitado. Shimoyama smoldering or chronic-favourable subtype of ATLL. Smoldering: ≥5% circulating abnormal lymphocytes, no organ involvement (skin/lung lesion permitted), LDH normal, BUN normal, albumin normal, no hypercalcemia, no lymphadenopathy or organomegaly. Chronic-favourable: similar to smoldering but lymphadenopathy/organomegaly permitted, LDH ≤2× ULN, BUN ≤ULN, albumin ≥ULN, Ca normal, no CNS/bone/GI/effusion. AZT+IFN-α (anti-HTLV-1 mechanism) yields 5-yr OS ~46% vs ~20% for chemotherapy in these subtypes (Bazarbachi 2010 meta-analysis, JNCI). Aggressive subtypes (acute/lymphoma/chronic-unfavourable) do NOT respond to AZT+IFN — route those to CHOEP+mogamulizumab via RF-ATLL-HIGH-RISK-BIOLOGY.

Sirolimus (rapamycin), an mTORC1 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (May 2015) and EMA-approved (2017) for treatment of LAM in adults. MILES phase III RCT (McCormack et al., NEJM 2011): N=89 (46 sirolimus, 43 placebo); 12-month treatment + 12-month observation. Primary endpoint: FEV1 change from baseline to 12 months (mL/month rate). FEV1 slope: +1 mL/month (sirolimus) vs -12 mL/month (placebo); difference 11 mL/month (p<0.001). Secondary: FVC improvement, VEGF-D reduction, 6-min walk improvement, QoL. After 12-month observation: benefits partially lost (FEV1 decline resumes), suggesting need for continuous therapy. mTOR inhibition does not eliminate LAM cells but controls their mTORC1-driven proliferation. Everolimus is used for TSC-associated LAM and for renal angiomyolipoma (EXIST-2). VEGF-D ≥800 pg/mL is a diagnostic biomarker (non-invasive diagnosis of LAM possible in right clinical context without biopsy).

Slowly dissolving lozenge releases nicot: Slowly dissolving lozenge releases nicotine across oral mucosa, producing a peak plasma level over ~20-30 minutes that blunts acute craving and withdrawal symptoms. Pharmacokinetics avoid the rapid arterial bolus that drives reinforcement from inhaled smoking. Cancer-prevention rationale: tobacco cessation reduces incidence of lung, head-and-neck, bladder, esophageal, pancreatic, cervical, kidney, AML, and other tobacco-attributable cancers (IARC Monograph 100E — Personal Habits and Indoor Combustions). NRT roughly doubles 6-month abstinence vs. placebo (Cochrane); combining a long-acting patch with a short-acting form (lozenge or gum) PRN improves quit rates over monotherapy. USPSTF Grade A for adult tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy.

Small-molecule PSMA-binding ligand conju: El ligando de unión a la PSMA de pequeñas moléculas conjugado con el radionucleido β-emitente Lu-177. El PSMA se expresa en >90% de las células de adenocarcinoma de próstata; el Lu-177-PSMA-617 se une al PSMA y entrega radioterapia citotóxica β directamente a los sitios tumorales. Requiere enfermedad positiva a la PET-PSAM para su selección (criterios de VISION).
Small-molecule allosteric inhibitor of m: Inhibidor alostérico de pequeñas moléculas de la enzima mutante IDH2 (R140Q, R172K hotspots). El mutante iDH2 cataliza la conversión neomórfica del α-cetoglutarato a 2-hidroxiglutalato (2-HG), un oncometabolito que impulsa la hipermetilación de ADN + histona y bloquea la diferenciación mieloide. Enasidenib reduce el 2-Hg, restaurando la desmetilacion dependiente de TE2 e induciendo la diferenciacion terminal de blastos leucémicos. Ago 2017 aprobado por la FDA sobre la base de datos de fase 1/2 de un solo brazo en R/R AML (AG221-AML-001).
Small-molecule inhibitor of the menin-KM: Small-molecule inhibitor of the menin-KMT2A (MLL) protein-protein interaction. KMT2A-rearranged and NPM1-mutated leukemias are dependent on menin recruitment to KMT2A-fusion or wild-type KMT2A complexes that drive aberrant HOXA / MEIS1 transcription. Disrupting menin-MLL displaces the leukemogenic transcriptional program, inducing differentiation and apoptosis of leukemic blasts. FDA-approved Nov 2024 on the basis of AUGMENT-101 phase 1/2 trial.

Sokal score (Sokal 1984) uses age, splee: Sokal score (Sokal 1984) uses age, spleen size, platelet count, blast %. High-risk (Sokal >1.2) marks ~20-25% of CML-CP at diagnosis with worse 10-yr OS and PFS on imatinib vs intermediate/low. ENESTnd (Saglio 2010) and DASISION (Kantarjian 2010) show 2nd-gen TKIs achieve faster + deeper molecular responses than imatinib in high-Sokal subgroups. ELN 2020 prefers ELTS (RF-CML-HIGH-RISK-ELTS, existing) but Sokal remains the more widely-used bedside score. Companion to RF-HASFORD-HIGH; both can fire together. Conflict- resolution: this RF intensifies toward 2nd-gen TKI; cardiotoxicity flags (RF-CML-COMORBIDITY-COMPLEX) may de-escalate back to imatinib.

La puntuación de sokal (Sokal 1984) utiliza edad, tamaño del bazo, recuento de plaquetas, % de blasto. El alto riesgo (Sokol > 1,2) marca ~20-25% de CML-CP al diagnóstico con peor OS de 10 años y PFS en imatinib vs intermedio/bajo. Enestnd (Saglio 2010) y DASI...

Somatic (tumor-only) BRCA1 or BRCA2 pathogenic variant identified on tumor NGS — pan-tumor PARPi-candidate signal. Disease applicability varies: ovarian (PAOLA-1, SOLO-1 — somatic BRCA pooled with germline in HRD-positive maintenance indication), mCRPC (PROfound cohort-A — olaparib mPFS 7.4 vs 3.6 mo, HR 0.34, somatic + germline pooled), pancreatic PDAC (POLO label is germline-only — somatic BRCA falls to off-label / NCCN "consider" tier), breast (OlympiAD / EMBRACA / OlympiA labels are germline-only — somatic BRCA breast remains investigational). Confirm somatic vs germline status via paired germline NGS before cascade-testing decisions (~40% of tumor-only "BRCA" calls are in fact germline per ASCO/CAP guidance).

Square-planar platinum(II) coordination: Square-planar platinum(II) coordination complex. After cellular uptake and aquation (Cl displaced by water in low-chloride intracellular environment), the activated species forms intra- and inter-strand DNA cross-links, predominantly 1,2-d(GpG) and 1,2-d(ApG) adducts. These adducts distort the DNA helix, blocking replication and transcription, and trigger apoptosis when not repaired. Resistance mechanisms include enhanced nucleotide excision repair, glutathione detoxification, and reduced cellular uptake (CTR1 transporter). Backbone for esophageal CRT, head-and-neck CRT, NSCLC, gastric (legacy), cervical, ovarian, testicular germ-cell, and bladder.

Standalone authoring of the cycle-1 step: La creación independiente del subprograma escalonado ciclo-1 para la administración subcutánea de epcoritamab. La secuencia escalonada — 0,16 mg → 0,8 mg → 48 mg — con prednisolona profiláctica 100 mg × 4 días alrededor de cada dosis suprime el SRC de cualquier grado hasta ~50% (predominantemente Grado 1-2; G≥3 ~3%) por EPCORE NHL-1. Entidad subregímen creada por separado para permitir la reutilización a través de las indicaciones DLBCL / FL / futuras y para proporcionar una única entidad para el render para la superficie del ciclo-1 hospital-monitoring + patrón de profilaxis corticosteróide. Combinar con el esquema de padres (REGIMEN-EPCORITAMB-MONO-DLBCl-3L) para el curso completo. Registro bibliográfico SRC-EPCORE-NHL-1-THIEBLEMONT-2023 está disponible; el vínculo de demanda clínica requiere doble firma clínica.
Standalone authoring of the obinutuzumab: Standalone authoring of the obinutuzumab single-dose pretreatment sub-regimen used to pre-deplete circulating CD20+ B-cells 7 days before glofitamab cycle 1 day 1. Mechanistically reduces CRS risk by shrinking the bispecific T-cell-engager substrate at first exposure; in NP30179 the combined obinutuzumab pretreatment + glofitamab step-up + corticosteroid premedication strategy held G≥3 CRS to ~4%. Sub-regimen entity authored separately for reuse across DLBCL / FL / future glofitamab combinations and to allow the renderer to surface the day -7 scheduling requirement as a distinct phase in patient-facing plans. Pair with parent schedule (REGIMEN-GLOFITAMAB-MONO-DLBCL-3L) starting 7 days later. Bibliographic record SRC-NP30179-DICKINSON-2022 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off.
Standard 12-week varenicline course is t: Standard 12-week varenicline course is the most effective single-agent tobacco-cessation pharmacotherapy (USPSTF + AHCPR). Set quit date day 8 of treatment (~end of titration). Extension to 24 weeks improves long-term abstinence in patients abstinent at 12 weeks. Counsel patients on neuropsychiatric monitoring (EAGLES 2016 reassured but residual caution).
Standard 1L cytoreduction for high-risk: Standard 1L cytoreduction for high-risk PV (age >60 OR prior thrombosis) AND high-risk ET (same criteria). Targets: - PV: Hct <45% (mainstay; CYTO-PV trial), platelets <400K - ET: platelets <400-450K Phlebotomy is the foundation in PV (with HU layered for cytoreduction); ASA at low dose unless contraindicated (extreme thrombocytosis with acquired vWD = relative contraindication). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive: Standard 1L for AML unfit for intensive 7+3 (VIALE-A: median OS 14.7 vs 9.6 mo for aza alone). TLS prophylaxis MANDATORY for first ramp cycle (5-week ramp not used in AML — accelerated 3-day ramp instead). Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor co-administration (azole prophylaxis) requires venetoclax dose reduction. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to: Standard 1L for MDS-HR (and bridging to alloHCT in eligible patients). Azacitidine and decitabine functionally equivalent; choice often local. Do NOT discontinue before cycle 6 unless overt progression — response is delayed. Ven+aza in HR-MDS is increasingly used (off-label extrapolation from VIALE-A AML data; no Phase-3 HR-MDS-specific RCT). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (t: Standard 1L for R/M HNSCC with CPS ≥1 (the majority of HNSCC). Locally advanced (curable) HNSCC routes to concurrent cisplatin + RT or surgery + adjuvant — separate algorithm not yet authored. HPV+ oropharyngeal R/M handled identically (no de-escalation in recurrent setting). Reuses pembrolizumab + cisplatin + carboplatin + 5-FU drug entities.
Standard 1L for advanced / metastatic GI: Standard 1L for advanced / metastatic GIST with imatinib-sensitive genotype (KIT exon 11 ~50%; KIT exon 9 ~10% — escalate to 800 mg; PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18; PDGFRA exon 12/14). Standard 1L for fit transplant-eligible: Estándar 1L para MCL apta para trasplante (edad <65, ECOG 0-1). Protocolo nórdico o estilo LYMA. Contribución principal: HiDAC + consolidación autoSCT + mantenimiento R mejoraron drásticamente la SLP (mediana >7-8 años vs ~3 años en R-CHOP solo). Riesgo de cardiotoxicidad + toxicidad acumulada de HiDac - selección de aptitud crítica.
Standard 1L for fit-for-intensive AML. A: Standard 1L for fit-for-intensive AML. Add midostaurin if FLT3-ITD/TKD+ (RATIFY: improved 4-y OS 51% vs 44%). Consolidation HiDAC 3 g/m² q12h d1, 3, 5 for 3-4 cycles in young fit favorable / intermediate-risk; alloHCT for adverse-risk in CR1. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 1L for low-risk CML chronic pha: Standard 1L for low-risk CML chronic phase, elderly, comorbid patients, or where cost / access is limiting. IRIS established imatinib 400 mg daily; 10-y OS ~83%. ELN 2020 milestones: ≤10% at 3 mo, ≤1% at 6 mo, ≤0.1% (MMR) at 12 mo. PCR monitoring q3mo for first year, then q3-6mo. TFR attempt eligible after ≥3 years on TKI + sustained DMR (MR4.5) ≥2 years per ELN. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.

Standard 1L for low/intermediate-risk AP: Standard 1L para APL de bajo/intermedio riesgo (Sanz WBC ≤10). APL0406: EFS de 2 años 97% vs 86% con ATRA+chemo (AIDA), OS 99% vs 91%, menos toxicidad hematológica, no cardiotoxicidad antraciclina. Standard 1L for the imatinib-sensitive G: La norma 1L para los genotipos GIST sensibles a imatinib (~85% de todos los GIST). Reutiliza la línea cruzada REG-IMATINIB-GIST-1L que codifica la regla de escalación de dosis del exón 9 del KIT.
Standard 1L for the ~50-100% of advanced: Estándar 1L para el ~50-100% de MTC avanzado que es RET-mutante (esporádico ~50% RET M918T; hereditario MEN2 ~100%). Reutiliza la enfermedad cruzada DRUG-SELPERCATINIB.
Standard 1L induction regimen for transp: Standard 1L induction regimen for transplant-eligible MM (4 cycles before harvest, then ASCT, then 2 cycles consolidation, then lenalidomide maintenance). For transplant-ineligible patients, VRd-lite (8-12 cycles, modified dosing per SWOG S0777) is the preferred 1L triplet. Standard-risk cytogenetics → VRd; high-risk → escalate to D-VRd (REG-DARA-VRD).
Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed: Standard 1L regimen for newly-diagnosed DLBCL NOS for the past 20+ years. ~60% cure rate overall, ~80% for low-IPI / ~55% for high-IPI. HBV screening + entecavir prophylaxis if HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ MANDATORY before first rituximab dose. Echocardiogram (LVEF) baseline + after cumulative dose >300 mg/m². Interim PET-CT after cycles 2-4 helpful for response assessment but doesn't routinely change therapy unless PD seen.
Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for: Standard 1L symptom-directed therapy for symptomatic PMF (and post-PV/ET MF). COMFORT-I/II: ≥35% spleen-volume reduction in ~42% vs 0.7% placebo; symptom improvement; pooled OS benefit suggested. Does NOT eliminate clone or alter natural history of fibrosis. AlloHCT remains the only curative option for fit intermediate-2 / high-risk patients. Momelotinib (MOMENTUM) preferred if anemia dominant; fedratinib (FREEDOM-2) 2L; pacritinib for severe thrombocytopenia. NEVER abrupt-stop. STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff before publication.
Standard 2L for SMZL/NMZL after rituxima: Estándar 2L para SMZL/NMZI después de la insuficiencia de rituximab en monoterapia. ORR ~85-90%; mediana de la SFP ~3-4 años. profilaxis PJP ≥6 mo post-anti-CD20; vigilancia obligatoria de reactivación del VHB.
Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progressio: Standard 2L mCRC after FOLFOX progression. Adding bevacizumab (TML / ML18147 trial) improves PFS (5.7 vs 4.1 mo) + OS (11.2 vs 9.8 mo, HR 0.81) over FOLFIRI alone. Anti-EGFR (cetuximab or panitumumab) alternative add-on for RAS-WT left-sided patients in 2L if not used in 1L (or if patient progressed on bevacizumab). UGT1A1 testing recommended before high-dose irinotecan use. Cholinergic syndrome vs delayed diarrhea — distinct pathophysiology + management.
Standard 2L+ for R/R FLT3-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ for R/R FLT3-mutated AML per ADMIRAL. Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — gilteritinib alone is not curative. Continue gilteritinib post-HCT as maintenance (off-label, supported by emerging data MORPHO trial). STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML pe: Standard 2L+ for R/R IDH2-mutated AML per AG221-AML-001 (FDA approval Aug 2017). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — enasidenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~14%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade) is biochemical UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic. Bibliographic record SRC-IDHENTIFY is available; SRC-AG221-AML-001 remains a source gap. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.
Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AM: Standard 2L+ for R/R KMT2A-rearranged AML per AUGMENT-101 (FDA approval Nov 2024). Bridge to alloHCT for fit candidates achieving CR/CRh — revumenib monotherapy is not curative; durable responses in trial were largely consolidated by alloHCT. Differentiation syndrome (~16%) is the signature AE — same dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib / enasidenib. QTc prolongation requires baseline + serial ECG. Bibliographic record SRC-AUGMENT-101 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. STUB — pending Co-Lead sign-off.

Standard 3-dose schedule (FDA / EMA hist: Standard 3-dose schedule (FDA / EMA historical labeling, age 9-25 F): 0, 1, 6 months. Each dose 0.5 mL IM in deltoid (preferred). WHO position 2017+: 2-dose schedule (0 and 6-12 months) acceptable for girls <15 y who are immunocompetent (single-dose alternative schedule under continued study in WHO/IARC SAGE 2022+). Catch-up: complete the 3-dose series in those who started but did not complete; do not restart if interrupted. Hepatic / renal impairment: no dose adjustment. Standard FLT3-ITD/TKD AML 1L (RATIFY tri: Standard FLT3-ITD/TKD AML 1L (ensayo RATIFY: mejor sistema operativo vs placebo cuando se añade a 7+3 + HiDAC). Tomar con alimentos para maximizar la biodisponibilidad. profilaxis antiemética esencial. Standard H2 component of chemotherapy pr: Standard H2 component of chemotherapy premedication, paired with H1 antihistamine (diphenhydramine) and corticosteroid (dexamethasone). Particularly important before paclitaxel (Cremophor vehicle hyper- sensitivity), rituximab, daratumumab, and other monoclonal antibodies with significant infusion reaction rates. Combined H1 + H2 blockade is empirically superior to H1 alone for prevention of mild-to-moderate hypersensitivity reactions (Lieberman-Goodyear, 2010). NEVER a substitute for epinephrine in true anaphylaxis — H1 + H2 + steroid treats pruritus, urticaria, mild bronchospasm, but does not reverse hypotension or upper airway edema. Famotidine preferred over cimetidine in oncology because of clean DDI profile (cimetidine inhibits multiple CYPs causing exposure increases of warfarin, theophylline, phenytoin, TKIs, vincristine — major hazard); ranitidine withdrawn worldwide 2019-2020 for NDMA contamination. CRITICAL: H2 antagonists raise gastric pH → reduce absorption of pH-dependent oral oncology agents (dasatinib, erlotinib, gefitinib, dabigatran, atazanavir) — separate by 2-10 h or substitute / time TKI dose. Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: Standard R-CHOP component. Premedication: 5-HT3 antagonist + dexamethasone. Mesna NOT routinely needed at R-CHOP doses (750 mg/m²) but mandatory for high-dose conditioning (>1500 mg/m²).
Standard TLS prophylaxis when initiating: Profilaxis estándar del TLS al iniciar la quimioinmunoterapia en pacientes con alta carga tumoral. Comience 24-48 horas antes del tratamiento.
Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomid: Standard VTE prophylaxis for lenalidomide-treated MM patients without additional VTE risk factors. For higher-risk patients (prior VTE, immobility, central venous catheter, active disease at induction) switch to LMWH (enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily) or apixaban. Hold aspirin if platelets <50K.

Standard adjunct for bronchospasm compon: Standard adjunct for bronchospasm component of anaphylaxis, chemotherapy infusion reactions, and CAR-T cytokine release syndrome — given concurrently with epinephrine (epinephrine remains the FIRST-LINE for true anaphylaxis with hypotension or upper airway edema). Nebulized 2.5-5 mg q20min × 3 then q1-4h is standard for moderate-severe bronchospasm. Critical: salbutamol does NOT reverse hypotension or upper airway edema — if these are present, epinephrine IM thigh is mandatory and urgent. Add ipratropium 500 µg nebulized if bronchospasm refractory or severe (combined β2 + muscarinic blockade). For bronchospasm during paclitaxel, rituximab, or monoclonal antibody infusions: stop infusion, administer salbutamol nebulized, diphenhydramine + famotidine + steroid as supportive — escalate to epinephrine if hypotension / upper airway involvement / no response in 5-10 min. Avoid in patients with cardiomyopathy / serious arrhythmia (QT-prolonging chemotherapy regimens particularly — TKIs, arsenic trioxide). Tachycardia and hypokalemia are dose-related — monitor in continuous nebulization. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU-covered.
Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusi: Standard adjunct for chemotherapy infusion reactions and severe anaphylaxis — given AFTER epinephrine IM (epinephrine is first-line, no substitute). Hydrocortisone's onset is delayed (4-6 h) so it prevents biphasic anaphylaxis recurrence rather than treating the acute event. Premedication for chemotherapy (e.g., taxanes, rituximab, daratumumab): typically dexamethasone 20 mg IV is used rather than hydrocortisone — dex is more potent (×30) per mg, has longer duration, lacks mineralocorticoid effect (less fluid retention), and dosing schedule is established. Hydrocortisone preferred over dex / methylprednisolone for: (1) adrenal insufficiency / crisis (mineralocorticoid activity matches physiological need); (2) septic shock with vasopressor refractoriness (300 mg/day approximately physiologic stress dose); (3) acute high-dose adjunct for refractory infusion reaction where mineralocorticoid effect supports hemodynamics. Single bolus of 100-200 mg has minimal long-term consequences — no taper needed for ≤3 days of acute use. Ukraine: cheap, ubiquitous, NSZU- covered.
Standard adjuvant for stage III colon, a: Adjuvante estándar para colon de estadio III, también de alto riesgo de estadios II (T4 / invasión linfovascular / < 12 LN muestra / pobremente diff). Metástico 1L para RAS-WT derecho O RAS mutante + bev (combinado con bevacizumab) — véase Indicación de la lógica biológica-add-on.

Standard adult dose: 800 mg PO once dail: Standard adult dose: 800 mg PO once daily continuous, taken on an empty stomach (≥1 hour before or ≥2 hours after a meal — food significantly increases exposure and toxicity risk). Dose reductions to 400 mg then 200 mg for grade 3-4 toxicity or hepatic AE per labelling. Treatment continued until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity. Standard adult monotherapy: 240 mg IV q2: Standard adult monotherapy: 240 mg IV q2w OR 480 mg IV q4w (over 30 min). Pediatric melanoma adjuvant (≥12 yrs, ≥40 kg): 240 mg q2w; <40 kg: 3 mg/kg q2w. With ipilimumab (1L melanoma, RCC, MSI-H CRC): nivolumab 1 mg/kg + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg q3w × 4 doses, then nivolumab 240 mg q2w or 480 mg q4w maintenance. CheckMate-649 (gastric 1L + chemo): 360 mg q3w with chemo or 240 mg q2w. CheckMate-577 (adjuvant esophageal post-CROSS without pCR): 240 mg q2w × 16 wks, then 480 mg q4w to total 1 year. Treatment until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or specified duration (1 yr adjuvant; 2 yrs metastatic in some indications).
Standard adult: 200 mg IV q3 weeks OR 40: Standard adult: 200 mg IV q3 weeks OR 400 mg IV q6 weeks (over 30 min). Pediatric: 2 mg/kg (up to 200 mg) IV q3w. Treatment continued until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or 24 months in most solid-tumor indications (35 cycles q3w). Adjuvant melanoma: 1 year (KEYNOTE-054). Neoadjuvant + adjuvant TNBC (KEYNOTE-522): 200 mg q3w × 8 cycles with chemo, then 9 cycles adjuvant. Neoadjuvant + adjuvant NSCLC (KEYNOTE-671): 200 mg q3w × 4 cycles with platinum-doublet, then 13 cycles adjuvant. Combination doses unchanged when paired with chemo, lenvatinib, axitinib, or trastuzumab.
Standard antibacterial prophylaxis in hi: Standard antibacterial prophylaxis in high-risk febrile neutropenia per IDSA / NCCN: anticipated ANC <100/µL ≥7 days (HSCT conditioning, AML induction, high-dose chemo for relapsed leukemia/lymphoma). Started day of conditioning / induction, continued through ANC recovery (>500/µL or marrow recovery). The Gram-positive enhancement vs ciprofloxacin (esp. viridans streptococcal mucositis-bacteremia prevention) is the rationale. Trade-offs: selects fluoroquinolone- resistant organisms over time (rising rates of ciprofloxacin/ levofloxacin-resistant E. coli and viridans streptococci limit benefit at some centers — local antibiogram critical); does NOT prevent invasive fungal infection (separate antifungal prophylaxis required — posaconazole, fluconazole). Standard 750 mg dose for pneumonia + Pseudomonas; 500 mg sufficient for FN prophylaxis. Diabetes: severe / fatal hypoglycemia signal — stricter monitoring. Class-wide FDA / EMA 2018 warning: avoid in uncomplicated infections. Ukraine: NSZU-covered for hematology prophylaxis indications; widely available.
Standard antiemetic premedication for mo: Standard antiemetic premedication for moderately/highly emetogenic chemotherapy (e.g., bendamustine).
Standard antifungal prophylaxis in HSCT: Standard antifungal prophylaxis in HSCT — pivotal trial (van Burik CID 2004) demonstrated superiority over fluconazole for invasive fungal infection prevention in HSCT recipients. Also first-line treatment for candidemia and invasive candidiasis (IDSA 2016 echinocandin recommendation). Differentiator from caspofungin: no loading dose, no body-weight adjustment, no hepatic adjustment in moderate impairment, even simpler DDI profile (no clinically meaningful interactions with cyclosporine or tacrolimus — key advantage in HSCT and solid-organ transplant where calcineurin inhibitors are concurrent). Boxed warning regarding hepatic tumors in rat carcinogenicity studies has not translated to human signal in two decades of post-marketing surveillance, but prescribing information warns against unnecessary prolonged use. Same spectrum limitations as caspofungin (no Mucor, no Cryptococcus, fungistatic for Aspergillus). Ukraine: registered, NSZU-covered; preferred echinocandin in HSCT contexts.

Standard bulky-disease definition adapte: Definición estándar de la enfermedad voluminosa adaptada a partir de las directrices sobre linfomas de células B.
Standard chemoimmunotherapy regimen for: Standard chemoimmunotherapy regimen for indolent B-cell lymphomas. In HCV-MZL, reserved for cases that are non-responsive to antiviral therapy or have aggressive/bulky disease at presentation requiring immediate cytoreduction.
Standard first-line empirical antibiotic: Standard first-line empirical antibiotic for febrile neutropenia (FN) per IDSA 2010 (Freifeld), ECIL-4, and NCCN — combines pseudomonal coverage, broad anaerobic activity, and acceptable toxicity profile. De-escalate after 48-72 h based on cultures (pip-tazo continued or narrowed to a directed agent). Add vancomycin if MRSA suspected (line infection, skin/soft-tissue source, prior MRSA colonization, hemodynamic instability) — but the pip-tazo + vanco combination has a debated AKI signal in adults (no signal in pediatrics or in CRRT). Common errors: under-dosing in CrCl 40-60 (still use 4.5 g q8h, not q12h), failure to extend infusion in critically ill patients (4-h infusion improves T>MIC), missing the rash → DRESS / SJS conversion early. Sodium load matters in heart failure — 4.5 g q6h delivers ~3 g sodium/ day. Ukraine: widely available; first-line FN empirical agent in hematology centers per local protocols aligned with NCCN/IDSA.
Standard for stage III unresectable post: Standard for stage III unresectable post-concurrent CRT. Pneumonitis G≥2 at end of CRT excludes durva initiation.
Standard for transfusion-dependent del(5: Estándar para el del(5q) LR-MDS dependiente de transfusión. ~56% alcanzan la independencia de transfusiones RBC (MDS-004); ~20-25% alcanza la CR citogenética (pérdida de clon del( 5q)). Prevención del embarazo obligatoria (programa REMS/Revlimid). profilaxis VTE obligatoria. Evite la combinación con ESA. STUB — pendiente de firma de Co-Lead.
Standard intensification for fit younger: Standard intensification for fit younger transplant-eligible PTCL NOS. Per Nordic NLG-T-01 + retrospective registry data: CHOEP superior to CHOP in younger T-cell patients; alloSCT consolidation in CR1 dramatically improves long-term PFS for poor-risk PTCL NOS (mature data from EBMT registries). AutoSCT alternative considered but generally inferior for PTCL NOS (vs B-cell NHL where autoSCT is durable). RIC alloSCT for older fit; myeloablative for younger. Donor selection critical — sibling > matched unrelated > haploidentical; GVHD prophylaxis individualized.
Standard neoadjuvant for HER2+ stage II-: Standard neoadjuvant for HER2+ stage II-III. pCR rate ~60-65% with TCHP. Path to KATHERINE-eligibility: residual disease post-neoadj → adjuvant T-DM1; pCR → continue trastuzumab + pertuzumab to 1 year total.
Standard of care for myeloma-related bon: Standard of care for myeloma-related bone disease — reduces skeletal- related events and pain. Calcium + vitamin D supplementation mandatory. Comprehensive dental evaluation BEFORE initiation; avoid invasive dental procedures during therapy. Monthly dosing for ≤2 years, then re-evaluate.
Standard of care for premenopausal HR+ a: Standard of care for premenopausal HR+ adjuvant. Switch to AI ± ovarian suppression after 2-5 years often considered. Postmenopausal: AI generally preferred but tamoxifen acceptable when AI contraindicated.
Standard pattern; entecavir/TDF prophyla: Patrón estándar; profilaxis entecavir/TDF de -7d a 12 mo post-anti-PD-1.

Standard salvage for chemosensitive r/r: Rescate estándar para la R/R PMBCL quimiosensible. Standard-track 2L for R/R SCLC. Topoteca: Standard-track 2L for R/R SCLC. CR + CRh rate 35% (95% CI 27-43); among CR + CRh responders, median DoR 25.9 mo, median time to CR + CRh 1.9 mo, 56-day mortality 8%. Mechanistically: olutasidenib is a more selective mutant-IDH1 inhibitor than ivosidenib (in vitro selectivity for mIDH1 R132 variants over WT-IDH1 / IDH2). QTc prolongation less frequent than ivosidenib in cross-trial. STUB pending Clinical Co-Lead sign-off. Substituted benzamide that antagonizes d: Benzamida sustituida que antagoniza los receptores D2 de la dopamina centralmente en la zona de desencadenamiento del quimiorreceptor (área postrema) y periféricamente en el tracto GI superior, reduciendo las náuseas y acelerando el vaciado gástrico. También un agonista de los receptores 5-HT4 (liberación potencial de acetilcolina en el plexo entérico → peristalsis aumentada) y a dosis altas (≥1 mg/kg) un antagonista de 5-HT3 débil. La acción proquinética la distingue de los antagonistas puros del D2 y es terapéuticamente útil para la gastroparesis inducida por quimioterapia, el vaciado gástrico tardío inducido por opioides y la dispepsia post-tratamiento. Aprobado por la FDA en 1979 para náuseas/vómitos y gastroparesia; ampliamente utilizado como antiemético avanzado en regímenes de NVCI. Uso restringido en 2009 (Aviso en caja de FDA) y 2013 (EMA) debido al riesgo de discinesia tardía con uso prolongado o de dosis altas.

Suicide enzyme-activated irreversible in: Inhibidor irreversible de ornitina decarboxilasa activado por enzimas suicidas (ODC), la primera enzima que limita la velocidad en la biosíntesis de poliaminas (putrescina → espermidina → espormina). La agotamiento de poliaminas suprime la proliferación celular. Razón de la prevención del cáncer: la ODC es un objetivo c-Myc; las poliamina PACES (Fase III, Meyskens et al.): eflorritina 500 mg + sulindac 150 mg PO diario redujo los adenomas metacrónicos en ~70% durante 36 meses en pacientes con adenamos esporádicos previos del colon (Cancer Prev Res 2008); seguimiento continuo. Aprobado por la FDA (Iwilfin, 2024) para la terapia de mantenimiento de neuroblastoma de alto riesgo — primera indicación oncológica para el agente.
Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbi: Sulfoxide prodrug reduced by gut microbiota and hepatic enzymes to active sulindac sulfide, which non-selectively inhibits COX-1 and COX-2, suppressing prostaglandin (especially PGE2) synthesis. Cancer- prevention rationale: COX-2 is upregulated in FAP adenomas; sulindac reduces polyp number and size in FAP (Giardiello NEJM 1993 RCT — 150 mg BID for 9 months, ~56% reduction in polyp number, ~65% in size; pooled trials in retained rectum post-colectomy show similar effect). PACES RCT (Meyskens 2008) combined eflornithine + sulindac reduced sporadic colorectal adenoma recurrence by ~70%. NOT FDA- labeled for chemoprevention; used off-label per NCCN Genetic Familial Colorectal 2025 in selected FAP patients (e.g., retained rectum, duodenal disease) under specialist hereditary-CRC team supervision.

La citoreducción completa (R0) mejora sustancialmente la SSP/OS — cuando se alcanza, la debultación primaria preferida. Synthetic broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone: La fluoroquinolona sintética de amplio espectro que inhibe dos topoisomerasas bacterianas esenciales tipo II: la ADN girosa (topoisomerasa II) — objetivo primario en bacterias Gram-negativas — y la topoisomerosa IV — objetivo principal en bacteria Gram positiva. La inhibición previene la supercarga o descarga de ADN necesaria para la replicación, transcripción y reparación, produciendo efecto bactericida con matanza dependiente de la concentración (AUC/MIC > 100 para Gram negativa). Excelente actividad vs Pseudomonas aeruginosa (mejor de las fluoroquinolonas más antiguas), Enterobacterales (incluyendo ESL en algunas regiones), Haemophilus, patógenos intracelulares (Legionella, Clamydia), micobacterias atípicas, Bacillus anthracis. Synthetic imidazoquinoline TLR7 agonist. Binds TLR7 on plasmacytoid dendritic cells and monocytes/macrophages, triggering NF-κB-mediated release of IFN-α, TNF-α, and other pro-inflammatory cytokines. Induces a local Th1-skewed innate + cell-mediated immune response against virally-infected or dysplastic epithelium; not directly cytotoxic or antiviral itself. Used topically for HPV-associated and field- cancerization lesions (external genital warts, actinic keratosis, superficial BCC) where local immune-mediated clearance is desired.
Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic: Synthetic monocyclic β-lactam antibiotic that binds penicillin- binding protein 3 (PBP-3) of aerobic Gram-negative bacilli with high affinity, inhibiting cell-wall synthesis and producing bactericidal effect. Activity narrowly restricted to aerobic Gram-negative bacteria including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Enterobacterales (most), Haemophilus, Neisseria. NO activity against Gram-positive bacteria, anaerobes, atypicals. Unique monobactam structure does NOT cross-react with penicillin or cephalosporin antibodies in IgE-mediated hypersensitivity, making aztreonam the preferred Gram-negative β-lactam for patients with documented severe penicillin allergy (including anaphylaxis). The exception is ceftazidime, which shares the aminothiazolyl side chain — patients with confirmed ceftazidime hypersensitivity may also react to aztreonam. FDA-approved 1986.

Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with g: Synthetic prostaglandin E1 analog with gastric mucosal protective effects (mucus + bicarbonate secretion, decreased gastric acid via enterochromaffin-like cell inhibition) and uterotonic activity. In oncology / cancer-prevention context: investigated as endometrial protection in tamoxifen users (theoretical rationale — endometrial PGE pathways). Evidence base is limited and inconsistent; not guideline-recommended for routine tamoxifen-associated endometrial protection. Primary FDA indications are NSAID-induced peptic ulcer prophylaxis and (off-label) obstetric uses.
Synthetic taurine analog with mixed acti: Analógico sintético de taurina con acción mixta en los receptores de glutamato NMDA (modulador) y neurotransmisión GABA alérgica. Restaura el balance inhibitorio glutamatérgico / GABa alérgico interrumpido por el uso de alcohol crónico. Utilizado para mantener la abstinencia en el trastorno del consumo de alcohol (DAU) después de una desintoxicación exitosa. Farmacoterapia de primera línea con DAU aprobada por la FDA junto con naltrexona y disulfiram. No hay efecto sobre la intoxicación o la abstención — mantenimiento puramente de la abstencia.
Synthetic tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloi: Synthetic tetrahydroisoquinoline alkaloid that binds the minor groove of DNA and stalls RNA polymerase II elongation, triggering RNAPII ubiquitination, double-strand breaks, and apoptosis selectively in transcription-addicted tumor cells. Also depletes tumor-associated macrophages. ATLANTIS (Phase III lurbinectedin + doxorubicin vs topotecan/CAV in 2L SCLC) failed its OS primary endpoint, but the pivotal single-arm Phase II Basket Study (NCT02454972, lurbinectedin monotherapy 3.2 mg/m² q21d) showed ORR 35% in 2L SCLC (CTFI ≥90 d ORR 45%; CTFI <90 d ORR 22%), supporting accelerated FDA approval Jun 2020.

T-ALL/T-LBL anterior mediastinal mass is: T-ALL/T-LBL anterior mediastinal mass is class-defining (~50-60% of T-ALL). Airway compromise + SVC syndrome are joint emergency presentations requiring HOLD on definitive induction — needs urgent steroids (prednisone or dexamethasone) to debulk, head-elevation, avoid supine GA. Per NCCN-BCELL ALL/LBL section: emergent steroid pre-phase before formal induction in symptomatic mediastinal mass. Per CALGB-10403: pediatric-inspired regimens begin with steroid pre-phase that addresses this. Direction HOLD because definitive induction is deferred until airway / SVC stabilized; priority 8 to win conflicts with TLS-emergency (which fires on the same patient). STUB — requires clinical co-lead signoff. Wiring suggestion: ALGO-T-ALL-1L step that branches on this RF to a steroid-pre-phase pathway before regimen selection.

TERT (Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase): TERT (Telomerase Reverse Transcriptase) is the catalytic subunit of telomerase. TERT promoter mutations (C228T or C250T, by chr5 coordinates) create de novo ETS family transcription factor binding sites, increasing TERT transcription and telomerase activity, extending cellular lifespan and enabling replicative immortality. Key clinical contexts: (1) Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC): TERT promoter mutations (~10–15% of PTC) are adverse prognostic markers, particularly when co-occurring with BRAF V600E (~8–12% of PTC). BRAF V600E + TERT promoter → mortality risk ~40× vs wild-type (Xing et al. NEJM 2014); this combination stratifies high-risk PTC requiring aggressive RAI and surveillance. (2) Follicular thyroid cancer: TERT mutations in ~15–20%. (3) GBM: TERT promoter mutations in ~70–80% (often co-occurring with EGFR amplification or IDH wild-type — defines molecular IDH-wild-type GBM). TERT mutation in IDH-wild-type astrocytoma with EGFR amplification or +7/-10 → WHO grade 4 GBM (CNS WHO 2021). TERT promoter mutations (C228T or C250T) occur in ~10–15% of papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) and ~15–20% of follicular thyroid cancer (FTC). TERT mutation is a strong adverse prognostic marker in differentiated thyroid cancer. Key evidence: Xing et al. (NEJM 2014 correspondence / JAMA Oncol): BRAF V600E + TERT promoter mutation creates a synergistic mortality risk — patients with both mutations have ~40× higher disease-specific mortality vs those with neither (BRAF+TERT double-positive: ~68% 10-yr mortality vs ~2% wild-type). TERT alone or BRAF alone: intermediate risk. ATA 2015 guidelines incorporate BRAF V600E as a risk-stratification factor; ESMO/NCCN 2025 updates recommend TERT testing alongside BRAF to identify the highest-risk PTC subgroup. Therapeutic implication: TERT-mutant/BRAF-mutant PTC should receive more aggressive radioiodine (RAI) therapy and enhanced surveillance. TERT promoter mutations are central to WHO CNS tumor classification (2021 5th edition): (1) GBM (IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4): TERT promoter mutation is one of three molecular defining features (together with EGFR amplification and chromosome +7/-10 copy number changes). An IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytoma with any of these features meets criteria for molecular GBM diagnosis regardless of histologic grade. TERT alone: ~70–80% of GBM. TERT mutation identifies the most aggressive tumor biology within IDH-wildtype astrocytomas. No TERT-directed therapy available. (2) Oligodendroglioma (IDH-mutant, 1p/19q co-deleted): TERT promoter mutation is present in ~70% and is part of the canonical molecular definition. TERT testing is used to confirm oligodendroglioma classification (IDH + 1p/19q + TERT triple positive). (3) IDH-mutant astrocytoma (grade 2–4): TERT promoter mutation is less common (~20%) and associated with worse prognosis within IDH-mutant tumors; CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion is the main grade 4 determinant in IDH-mutant astrocytoma. Standard treatment for GBM is unchanged by TERT status: Stupp protocol (RT + temozolomide, followed by temozolomide maintenance). MGMT promoter methylation — not TERT — determines temozolomide sensitivity. ESCAT IIB: TERT is a diagnostic molecular classifier in glioma with strong prognostic significance but no actionable therapeutic target.

TGCT is classified as locally aggressive: TGCT is classified as locally aggressive (diffuse-type) or benign (localized). Despite benign histology, diffuse-type TGCT (formerly PVNS) causes severe joint destruction, pain, and functional disability, with high surgical recurrence rates (25–50%). Pexidartinib (CSF1R inhibitor) is the only FDA-approved systemic therapy (2019, ILLUMINATE trial): ORR 38%, durable response in responders, but significant hepatotoxicity risk (REMS program; transaminase monitoring mandatory). Surgery remains the primary modality; pexidartinib is reserved for patients with severe morbidity not amenable to surgery improvement. Malignant TGCT (9252/3) is extremely rare.
THOR (Loriot NEJM 2023) phase 3, cohort: THOR (Loriot NEJM 2023) phase 3, cohort 1: erdafitinib 8 mg PO daily (with up-titration to 9 mg if phosphate <5.5 mg/dL day 14) vs investigator-choice chemotherapy (docetaxel OR vinflunine) in metastatic urothelial carcinoma with selected FGFR2/3 alterations (mutation S249C / R248C / G370C / Y373C OR FGFR2/3 fusion), after ≥1 prior line including PD-(L)1 inhibitor (n=266; 136 erda vs 130 chemo). Met primary endpoint mOS 12.1 vs 7.8 mo (HR 0.64, p=0.005), mPFS 5.6 vs 2.7 mo (HR 0.58), ORR 35.3% vs 8.5%. THOR cohort 2 (erda vs pembrolizumab in PD-(L)1-naive) was negative and not used to support labeling. FDA converted accelerated to full approval Jan 2024 based on THOR cohort 1. Class toxicity: hyperphosphatemia (~76%), nail toxicity (~57%), stomatitis, central serous retinopathy (~25%, usually reversible). STUB pending Clinical Co-Lead sign-off. TMPRSS2-ERG fusion detected on tumor RNA: TMPRSS2-ERG fusion detected on tumor RNA / FISH / IHC for ERG in localized or metastatic prostate cancer — INFORMATIONAL prognostic signal. Most common recurrent gene fusion in prostate cancer (~40-50% of localized PCa, ~15-30% of mCRPC). Conflicting prognostic literature: some series report worse PSA-relapse-free survival post-prostatectomy, others report no independent prognostic value after adjusting for Gleason / PSA / stage. NO predictive role established for ARSI, PARPi, taxane, or radioligand selection — does NOT modify treatment algorithm. Surfaces in MDT brief as: (1) molecular subtyping context, (2) potential clinical-trial enrollment criterion (ERG-positive cohorts in some experimental studies), (3) helpful for confirming prostate origin in metastatic-of-unknown-primary workup (TMPRSS2-ERG is highly prostate-specific).

TMPRSS2-ERG is the most common gene fusi: TMPRSS2-ERG is the most common gene fusion in prostate cancer (~50% of Caucasian prostate adenocarcinomas, ~20-30% in Asian and African-American populations — frequency varies by ancestry). Mechanism: androgen-responsive TMPRSS2 promoter drives aberrant ERG expression after interstitial 21q22 deletion (~2/3 of cases) or translocation. Clinical relevance: PROGNOSTIC, not Tx-modifying. Original Tomlins 2005 (Science) report linked fusion to aggressive disease; subsequent meta-analyses (e.g., Pettersson 2012, Cancer Epidemiol Biomarkers Prev) showed prognostic signal weaker than initially claimed and confounded by Gleason / stage. PARPi-sensitivity hypothesis (ETS-fusions causing replicative stress → PARPi response) TESTED but not validated as a monotherapy biomarker — ERG status alone does NOT qualify for olaparib / niraparib / talazoparib (which require HRR mutations). Use in KB: ships as biomarker only — no IND, no algorithm step. May be used in MDT brief to confirm prostate- origin in challenging metastasis-of-unknown-primary cases (ERG-IHC in metastasis = strong prostate-origin signal). La enfermedad EGFR-mutante o rearrastada con ALK responde POORMENTE a la IC incluso en TPS-100% — el objetivo del conductor TKI es siempre el 1L. TPS 1-49% — quimiología + ICI combo (KEYNOTE-189 no escamoso, KEYNOSTE-407 escamosa) preferido; la monoterapia con pembrolizumab sigue siendo una opción (KeyNOTE-042) pero inferior a la combo. La comutación STK11/KEAP1 es un predictor negativo para la respuesta a IC incluso en el TPS alto — biomarcador emergente para la quimio-cirugía + IC combinada sobre monoterapia. TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866): Phase II: TROPION-Breast01 (NCT05104866): Phase III, HR+/HER2- metastatic breast post-ET + 1-2 prior chemo lines. Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg q3w vs investigator-choice chemo (eribulin / vinorelbine / gemcitabine / capecitabine). Median PFS 6.9 vs 4.9 mo (HR 0.63). FDA approval Jan 2025 (Datroway). Distinguishing AE profile vs T-DXd: higher stomatitis + ocular toxicity, lower (~3% vs ~12%) ILD rate. TROP2-IHC not required as predictive biomarker per current label (broad-eligibility design). When HER2-low IHC 1+ / 2+ ISH- coexists, T-DXd (DESTINY-Breast04 PFS 10.1 vs 5.4 mo, HR 0.51) is preferred over Dato-DXd by efficacy margin; Dato-DXd is the option for IHC-0 (HER2-zero) patients ineligible for T-DXd. Bibliographic record SRC-TROPION-BREAST01-BARDIA-2024 is available; clinical claim linkage requires dual clinical sign-off. UA access: not registered; named-patient import / EAP only.

TSC1 (hamartin) forms a heterodimeric co: TSC1 (hamartin) forms a heterodimeric complex with TSC2 (tuberin) that acts as a GTPase activating protein (GAP) for Rheb, maintaining mTORC1 in an inactive state. Loss of either TSC1 or TSC2 → constitutive mTORC1 activation → protein synthesis, cell growth, proliferation. Clinical manifestations of TSC1 loss: (1) Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — germline TSC1 (~30%) or TSC2 (~70%): cortical tubers, SEGA, renal AML, cardiac rhabdomyomas, LAM (females), skin lesions. TSC1 germline associated with milder phenotype than TSC2. (2) LAM — predominantly somatic TSC2 (>80%) or rarely TSC1 in sporadic LAM. TSC-associated LAM has germline TSC mutation. (3) Renal angiomyolipoma (sporadic) — somatic TSC1/TSC2 in ~50%. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) are approved for multiple TSC/LAM manifestations: - Sirolimus: LAM (MILES 2011; FDA 2015) - Everolimus: SEGA (EXIST-1), renal AML (EXIST-2), TSC-related seizures (EXIST-3); renal cell carcinoma (SRC-BOLERO2-BASELGA-2012 — different indication via PIK3/AKT/mTOR pathway). Note: the BIO entity covers TSC1 specifically; TSC2 mutations are clinically similar but a separate gene — both treated with mTOR inhibitors.

TSC1 germline pathogenic variants drive Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — an mTOR-pathway hyperactivation syndrome with multi-organ tumor predisposition: subependymal giant cell astrocytoma (SEGA), renal angiomyolipomas (AML), lymphangioleiomyomatosis (LAM, females), cardiac rhabdomyomas, and cortical tubers. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per Tuberous Sclerosis Complex Consensus Conference / NCCN CNS): brain MRI q1-3y through age 25 for SEGA, renal MRI/US q1-3y from diagnosis (lifelong) for AML, pulmonary function tests + HRCT chest q5-10y in adult females for LAM, baseline echocardiogram + ECG, dermatology and ophthalmology exam annually. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) are active across SEGA, growing renal AMLs (≥3 cm), and LAM — these are surveillance-triggered interventions, not prophylactic. TSC2 germline pathogenic variants drive Tuberous Sclerosis Complex (TSC) — the more clinically severe of the two TSC genotypes (TSC2 carriers have earlier onset and broader phenotype than TSC1). Same multi-organ tumor spectrum as TSC1: SEGA, renal AML (typically more numerous and earlier in TSC2), LAM, cardiac rhabdomyoma, cortical tubers. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol identical to TSC1 (per TSC Consensus Conference 2012 + 2021 update / NCCN CNS): brain MRI q1-3y through age 25 for SEGA, renal MRI/US q1-3y lifelong, PFT + HRCT chest q5-10y in adult females, baseline echocardiogram, annual dermatology + ophthalmology exam. Contiguous-gene TSC2/PKD1 deletions present with severe polycystic kidney disease in addition to AML and require nephrology co-management. mTOR inhibitors (everolimus, sirolimus) active across SEGA, renal AML ≥3 cm, and LAM. ESCAT IIA.

Tazemetostat (EPZ-6438), an EZH2 methyltransferase inhibitor, is FDA-approved (January 2020) for adults and pediatric patients (≥16 years) with metastatic or locally advanced epithelioid sarcoma not eligible for complete resection. This was the first FDA approval in this disease and the first EZH2-targeted approval in solid tumors. EZH-202 phase II (Gounder et al., Lancet Oncology 2020): N=62 evaluable; primary endpoint ORR by RECIST 1.1. ORR: 15% (9/62; 1 CR, 8 PR); clinical benefit rate (CR+PR+SD ≥32 weeks): 26%. mDOR in responders: not reached at time of analysis. Disease control rate: ~26% with durable SD. Safety profile: generally well-tolerated; rare secondary T-cell lymphoma risk (class-wide EZH2 inhibitor concern); myeloid malignancy risk with long-term use (monitoring recommended). INI1 loss (IHC) is the companion diagnostic — required for diagnosis and eligibility. Standard chemotherapy (doxorubicin-based) remains an option for fit patients with rapidly progressive disease; tazemetostat preferred for slow-growing/indolent course.

Testicular GCT is the most common solid: Testicular GCT is the most common solid tumor in men aged 15-35 and one of the most curable cancers even at metastatic stage (BEP-based chemotherapy cures ~80-92% of metastatic good/intermediate-risk GCT; ~50% poor-risk). Early diagnosis via self-examination + ultrasound is critical. All staging workup requires serum AFP, beta-hCG, LDH at diagnosis and post-orchiectomy to determine marker trajectory. RPLND (retroperitoneal lymph node dissection) is used for: residual masses after chemotherapy (seminoma → PET-guided; NSGCT → surgery for >1cm residual), pathologic stage I NSGCT surveillance-alternative.
Testicular GCT is unique — curative even: Testicular GCT is unique — curative even at metastatic stage for most patients. Post-BEP residual mass management: seminoma >3cm → PET-guided (FDG-avid → biopsy/resection; FDG-negative → observe); NSGCT >1cm → RPLND for residual teratoma resection. Surveillance after good-risk GCT: CT CAP q3-4 months year 1, then q6 months year 2-3; markers q1-2 months year 1. 2L salvage: TIP (paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin) or VIP (vinblastine + ifosfamide + cisplatin) for cisplatin-sensitive relapse; high-dose chemotherapy + ASCT at specialized centers for multiply relapsed/refractory GCT.

Tetracycline binds reversibly to the 30S: Tetracycline binds reversibly to the 30S ribosomal subunit at the A site, preventing aminoacyl-tRNA from associating with the ribosome and blocking the elongation step of bacterial protein synthesis. Bacteriostatic. Broad spectrum: Gram-positives, Gram-negatives, atypicals (Mycoplasma, Chlamydia, Rickettsia), spirochetes, Helicobacter pylori (including metronidazole- and clarithromycin-resistant strains in PBMT quadruple therapy). Distinct from doxycycline (semi-synthetic, longer half-life, better tissue penetration) — but cheaper and historically the canonical PBMT component.

The learning path starts after histology: The learning path starts after histology confirms DLBCL NOS. The learning path starts after histology confirms invasive breast carcinoma with metastatic disease. Before any first-line plan is drafted the chapter expects a complete ER/PR result, a HER2 result that captures the HER2-low band (IHC 1+ or 2+ ISH-negative) for later 2L options, germline BRCA1/2 testing, an ECOG/fitness summary, baseline LVEF and ECG before any drug with cardiac risk, and brain imaging when CNS symptoms are present. The vast majority of BCCs are cured with: The vast majority of BCCs are cured with surgery or radiation. Hedgehog inhibitors (vismodegib, sonidegib) are approved only for locally advanced unresectable or metastatic BCC — a small fraction of all BCCs. Gorlin syndrome (PTCH1 germline) warrants genetic counseling and lifelong surveillance. SMO inhibitors cause significant side effects (muscle cramps, alopecia, dysgeusia, weight loss) limiting long-term use. Cemiplimab (anti-PD-1) is FDA-approved for locally advanced/metastatic BCC after HHI failure.

Therapeutic radioiodine (I-131) exposure for differentiated thyroid cancer (DTC) ablation/treatment OR Graves' disease — cumulative doses ≥100 mCi (3.7 GBq) lifetime confer small-but-real increased risk of secondary malignancies. Strongest signal: leukemia (RR ~1.5-2.0 above population baseline; latency 2-10 years), salivary gland cancer (RR ~1.3-2.0; latency 5-15 years), breast cancer in females (RR ~1.2-1.4; lower-quality evidence, dose-dependent), bladder cancer (modest signal). Iodine concentrates in salivary glands + stomach + bladder during excretion; non-target dose drives secondary cancer signal. Risk modestly higher at younger ages of exposure (proliferating tissues more radiosensitive). Prevention- persona RedFlag (§20, v0.3 iatrogenic expansion).

Thienobenzodiazepine atypical antipsycho: Thienobenzodiazepine atypical antipsychotic with high-affinity antagonism at multiple receptors implicated in nausea and vomiting: dopamine D2 (mesolimbic), serotonin 5-HT2A/2C, histamine H1, muscarinic M1, and α1-adrenergic. Multi-receptor blockade in the vomiting center, area postrema, and chemoreceptor trigger zone produces broad-spectrum antiemetic effect across acute, delayed, and breakthrough CINV phases. Adding olanzapine 10 mg PO days 1-4 to triple antiemetic prophylaxis (NK1 + 5-HT3 + dex) improves complete-response rate by ~10% absolute for HEC (Navari, NEJM 2016). Particularly effective for refractory or breakthrough nausea where single-receptor antagonists have failed. Approved by FDA September 1996 (psychiatric indications); CINV use is guideline-supported off-label / on-label depending on jurisdiction.

Third of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder: Third of three Ashkenazi Jewish founder mutations (combined carrier frequency ~2.5% in AJ; ~1.5% for this BRCA2 variant alone in some cohorts). Single-T deletion in exon 11 causing frameshift and premature termination in the DNA-binding domain region — abolishes RAD51-mediated homologous-recombination repair. Modern HGVS notation c.5946delT; legacy notation 6174delT (older mRNA-numbering convention). Lifetime cancer risks consistent with BRCA2 average: breast ~50-60%, ovarian ~15-20%, male breast ~6-8%, pancreas ~5-7%, prostate ~20-25%. Higher pancreas risk than BRCA1 — CAPS-Consortium pancreatic surveillance (annual MRI/MRCP or EUS from age 50 or 10 years before youngest PDAC in family) applies to BRCA2 carriers with PDAC family history. Same breast/ovarian surveillance and risk-reduction protocols as other BRCA2 pathogenic variants (annual MRI from 25-30, RRSO 40-45). NCCN 2025 endorses population-wide AJ founder-panel testing. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

This regimen models the mandatory preope: This regimen models the mandatory preoperative alpha-adrenergic blockade step described in the Disease narrative -- NOT a cytotoxic or antineoplastic regimen. Three anatomically and biologically dist: Three anatomically and biologically distinct subtypes; actionable alterations cluster in intrahepatic. Resectable: surgery + adjuvant capecitabine 6 months (BILCAP). Liver transplant for selected pCCA after Mayo neoadjuvant protocol (chemo-radiation + brachy → exam-under-anesthesia → transplant). Advanced 1L: gemcitabine + cisplatin + durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) replaced gem-cis monotherapy as standard. Pembrolizumab + gem-cis is an alternative (KEYNOTE-966). Advanced 2L+ by genotype (intrahepatic CCA enrichment): - FGFR2 fusion / rearrangement (~10–20% iCCA): pemigatinib (FIGHT-202) or futibatinib (FOENIX-CCA2) — both FDA-approved. Hyperphosphatemia is on-target effect. - IDH1 R132 (~15% iCCA): ivosidenib (ClarIDHy) — modest PFS benefit. - HER2 IHC 3+ / amplified (~5–10% perihilar/distal): trastuzumab + pertuzumab (MyPathway) or trastuzumab deruxtecan (DESTINY-PanTumor02); zanidatamab (HERIZON-BTC-01). - BRAF V600E (~5%): dabrafenib + trametinib (ROAR — tumor-agnostic). - MSI-H / dMMR (~2–3%): pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-158). - NTRK fusion (rare): larotrectinib / entrectinib. Three distinct entities under \"ALCL\" u: Three distinct entities under "ALCL" umbrella: systemic ALCL ALK+, systemic ALCL ALK-, primary cutaneous ALCL (separate disease, indolent). Breast-implant-associated ALCL is fourth distinct WHO 5th-ed entity (rare; treatment surgical + adjuvant). All CD30+ → brentuximab-CHP (ECHELON-2) preferred over CHOP for systemic disease.
Three subsites with distinct biology and: Three subsites with distinct biology and treatment patterns. Early glottic (T1-T2N0): radiation OR transoral laser microsurgery (TLM) — both ~90% local control with voice preservation as key endpoint. Locally advanced: larynx-preservation chemoradiation (cisplatin + RT) per RTOG 91-11 / VA-trial paradigm vs total laryngectomy + postoperative RT — patient preference / fitness drives choice. Recurrent / metastatic: pembrolizumab ± chemo per KEYNOTE-048 (same framework as broader HNSCC). Smoking cessation surveillance dominates prevention narrative.
Three-marker screening before B-cell-dep: Three-marker screening before B-cell-depleting or anti-CD38 therapy: HBsAg (current infection), anti-HBc total (past or occult infection), anti-HBs (immunity). HBV-DNA quantitative PCR follows when HBsAg+ or anti-HBc+ to distinguish active vs resolved infection.

Thymidine analog; intracellularly phosph: Analógico de la timidina; fosforilado intracelularmente por la timidina quinasa/timidilato quinasis/difosfato quinaso nucleósido a la ZDV-trifosfato, que compite con el dTTP para la transcriptasa inversa VIH-1 / HTLV-1 y actúa como un terminador de cadena obligatorio (falta de 3'-OH para una mayor alargamiento). En la leucemia / linfoma de células T adultas (ATLL) impulsada por HTLV-1, AZT combinada con IFN-α ejerce actividad antineoplásica no sólo atribuible a la inhibición de la transcriptasa inversa: induce apoptosis a través de supresión de la vía NF-κB, reduce la regulación de la unidad de ciclo celular HTIV-1 Mediado por impuestos, y se sinergiza con la señalización antiproliferativa del interferón tipo I (Metaanálisis de Bazarbachi 2010: ~50% de CR duradera en ATLL indolente).
Thyroglobulin doubling time <12 months i: El tiempo de duplicación de la tiroglobulina < 12 meses es un marcador pronóstico adverso validado (Miyauchi et al, JCEM 2011) — predice una SG más corta en DTC. Refractoresidad RAI definida según los criterios de ATA (Consenso de Schlumberger): no captación al diagnóstico, captación de nivel de lesión, pero sin respuesta o progresión después de RAI ≥ 600 mCi acumulativo.
